title.zh: 新唐書卷七十二 表第十二上 宰相世系二上

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 長孫長孫氏出自拓拔鬱律。

translations.literal: The Zhangsun clan of the Zhangsun surname was traced to Tuoba Yulu.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhangsun clan descended from Tuoba Yulu.

sentences.zh: 生二子：長曰沙莫雄，次曰什翼犍。

translations.literal: He bore two sons: the elder was called Shamoxiong, the younger was called Shiyujian.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons—the elder, Shamoxiong, and the younger, Shiyujian.

sentences.zh: 什翼犍即後魏道武皇帝祖也。

translations.literal: Shiyujian was the ancestor of Emperor Daowu of the Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyujian was the forebear of Emperor Daowu of Later Wei.

sentences.zh: 後魏法，七分其國人，以兄弟分統之。

translations.literal: By Later Wei law, the people of the state were divided into seven parts, and brothers were assigned to govern them separately.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Wei custom, the realm's population was split into seven shares, with brothers placed over each in separate command.

sentences.zh: 沙莫雄為南部大人，後改名仁，號為拓拔氏。

translations.literal: Shamoxiong served as Great Man of the South; later his name was changed to Ren, and he was styled of the Tuoba clan.
translations.idiomatic: Shamoxiong held the post of Great Man of the South; he later took the name Ren and was styled of the Tuoba clan.

sentences.zh: 生嵩，太尉、柱國大將軍、北平宣王。

translations.literal: He bore Song, Grand Commandant, Pillar-of-State Grand General, Prince Xuan of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Song, Grand Commandant, Pillar-of-State Grand General, and Prince Xuan of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 道武以嵩宗室之長，改為長孫氏。

translations.literal: Daowu, because Song was the eldest of the imperial clan, changed [the surname] to Zhangsun.
translations.idiomatic: Because Song was the senior member of the imperial clan, Daowu changed the surname to Zhangsun.

sentences.zh: 至孝文，以獻帝長兄為紇骨氏，次兄普氏為周氏，又次兄為達奚氏，又次兄為伊婁氏，改為婁氏，又次兄敦丘氏為丘氏，次兄俟氏為万俟氏，叔公之後乙旃氏為叔孫氏，疏屬車焜氏改為車氏，是為十姓。

translations.literal: When it came to Xiaowen, the Presentation Emperor's eldest elder brother was made the Hegu clan; the next elder brother of the Pu clan was made the Zhou clan; the next again was made the Daxi clan; the next again was the Yilou clan, changed to the Lou clan; the next again, the Dunqiu clan was made the Qiu clan; the next elder brother, the Si clan was made the Moqi clan; descendants of the uncle-grandfather, the Yizhan clan was made the Shusun clan; a distant kinsman, the Che Kun clan was changed to the Che clan—these were the ten surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiaowen, the Presentation Emperor's eldest elder brother was made the Hegu clan; the next elder brother of the Pu line became the Zhou clan; another became the Daxi clan; another, the Yilou clan, was changed to Lou; another, the Dunqiu clan, became Qiu; the next elder brother of the Si line became Moqi; descendants of the uncle-grandfather, the Yizhan clan, became Shusun; and a distant kinsman of the Che Kun line was changed to Che—these were the ten surnames.

sentences.zh: 太和中，詔自代北而徙者皆為河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, an edict declared that all who had migrated from north of Dai were to be registered as natives of Henan and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe reign, an edict declared that everyone who had moved south from north of Dai was to be registered as a native of Henan and Luoyang.

translations.literal: Song had three sons: Tai, Tong, and Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Song had three sons: Tai, Tong, and Dun.

sentences.zh: 泰，征南將軍、都督中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: Tai, General Who Campaigns South, Director of All Military Affairs at Home and Abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Tai served as General Who Campaigns South and Director of All Military Affairs at Home and Abroad.

sentences.zh: 生黃門侍郎、大將軍延年。

translations.literal: He bore Yannian, Yellow Gate Attendant, Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son, Yannian, who served as Yellow Gate Attendant and Grand General.

sentences.zh: 延年生陝州刺史、鄫國公儉，儉生相州刺史、昌寧公平。

translations.literal: Yannian bore Jian, Governor of Shanzhou, Duke of Zeng; Jian bore Ping, Governor of Xiangzhou, Duke of Changning.
translations.idiomatic: Yannian's son was Jian, Governor of Shanzhou and Duke of Zeng; Jian's son was Ping, Governor of Xiangzhou and Duke of Changning.

translations.literal: Two sons: Daosheng and Daokai.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Daosheng and Daokai.

translations.literal: Daosheng, Grand Commandant, Prince Jing of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng served as Grand Commandant and Prince Jing of Shangdang.

translations.literal: Three sons: Zhan, Taiyi, and Deyi.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Zhan, Taiyi, and Deyi.

sentences.zh: 旃，司空、上黨康王， 生觀。

translations.literal: Zhan, Minister of Works, Prince Kang of Shangdang; he bore Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan served as Minister of Works and Prince Kang of Shangdang; his son was Guan.

sentences.zh: 觀，司徒、上黨定王，生稚、澄。

translations.literal: Guan, Minister over the Masses, Prince Ding of Shangdang; he bore Zhi and Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Guan served as Minister over the Masses and Prince Ding of Shangdang; he had two sons, Zhi and Cheng.

sentences.zh: 稚字幼卿，西魏尚書令、太師、上黨文宣王。

translations.literal: Zhi, styled Youqing, Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing of Western Wei, Grand Preceptor, Prince Wenhuan of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, styled Youqing, served Western Wei as Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing and Grand Preceptor, and held the title Prince Wenhuan of Shangdang.

translations.literal: Two sons: Ziyu and Ziyan.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Ziyu and Ziyan.

sentences.zh: 子裕，右武衞將軍、平原公。

translations.literal: Ziyu, General of the Right Martial Guard, Duke of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu served as General of the Right Martial Guard and Duke of Pingyuan.

translations.literal: Two sons: Shaoyuan and Si.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Shaoyuan and Si.

translations.literal: Of the Zhangsun clan, one chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhangsun clan produced one chief minister.

translations.literal: Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji.

sentences.zh: 杜杜氏出自祁姓，帝堯裔孫劉累之後。

translations.literal: The Du clan of the Du surname was traced to the Qi surname; they were descendants of Liu Lei, collateral descendant of Emperor Yao.
translations.idiomatic: The Du clan descended from the Qi surname and traced its line to Liu Lei, a collateral descendant of Emperor Yao.

sentences.zh: 在周為唐杜氏，成王滅唐，以封弟叔虞，改封唐氏子孫於杜城，京兆杜陵縣是也。

translations.literal: In Zhou times they were the Tang-Du clan. King Cheng destroyed Tang and enfeoffed his younger brother Shuyu; the descendants of the Tang clan were moved to Ducheng—this is Dulings County in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou they were known as the Tang-Du clan. When King Cheng destroyed Tang and enfeoffed his younger brother Shuyu, the descendants of the Tang line were resettled at Ducheng—the present Dulings County in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 杜伯入為宣王大夫，無罪被殺，子孫分適諸侯之國，居杜城者為杜氏。

translations.literal: Duke Du entered [Zhou] to serve as Grand Master under King Xuan; he was executed though guiltless. His descendants dispersed to the lands of various feudal lords; those who settled at Ducheng became the Du clan.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Du entered Zhou service as Grand Master under King Xuan and was executed though innocent. His descendants scattered to the domains of various feudal lords; those who remained at Ducheng became the Du clan.

sentences.zh: 在魯有杜洩，避季平子之難，奔於楚，生大夫綽。

translations.literal: In Lu there was Du Xie, who fled the troubles of Ji Pingzi and went to Chu; he bore the Grandee Chuo.
translations.idiomatic: In Lu there was Du Xie, who fled the troubles raised by Ji Pingzi and took refuge in Chu; his son was the Grandee Chuo.

sentences.zh: 綽生段，段生赫，赫為秦大將軍，食采於南陽衍邑，世稱為「杜衍」。

translations.literal: Chuo bore Duan, Duan bore He; He served as Grand General of Qin and received his fief at Yanyi in Nanyang, and for generations they were called "Du of Yan."
translations.idiomatic: Chuo's son was Duan, and Duan's son was He. He served Qin as Grand General and held a fief at Yanyi in Nanyang; for generations the line was known as "Du of Yan."

sentences.zh: 赫少子秉，上黨太守，生南陽太守札。

translations.literal: His youngest son Bing was Governor of Shangdang; he bore Zha, Governor of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Bing served as Governor of Shangdang; his son Zha became Governor of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 札生周，御史大夫，以豪族徙茂陵。

translations.literal: Zha bore Zhou, Censor-in-Chief; as a powerful clan they were moved to Maoling.
translations.idiomatic: Zha's son Zhou served as Censor-in-Chief; as a powerful clan, the family was relocated to Maoling.

translations.literal: Three sons: Yanshou, Yankao, and Yannian.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Yanshou, Yankao, and Yannian.

sentences.zh: 延年字幼公，御史大夫、建平敬侯。

translations.literal: Yannian, styled Yougong, Censor-in-Chief, Marquis Jing of Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: Yannian, styled Yougong, served as Censor-in-Chief and held the title Marquis Jing of Jianping.

translations.literal: Six sons: Huan, Ji, Ta, Shao, Xu, and Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: Huan, Ji, Ta, Shao, Xu, and Xiong.

sentences.zh: 熊字少卿，荊州刺史，生後漢諫議大夫穰，字子饒。

translations.literal: Xiong, styled Shaoqing, Governor of Jingzhou; he bore Rang of Later Han, Remonstrance and Discussion Grand Master, styled Ziyao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong, styled Shaoqing, served as Governor of Jingzhou; his son was Rang of Later Han, Remonstrance and Discussion Grand Master, styled Ziyao.

translations.literal: Two sons: Dun and Du.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Dun and Du.

sentences.zh: 敦字仲信，西河太守，生邦，字召伯，中散大夫。

translations.literal: Dun, styled Zhongxin, Governor of Xihe; he bore Bang, styled Zhaobo, Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Dun, styled Zhongxin, served as Governor of Xihe; his son was Bang, styled Zhaobo, a Palace Attendant.

translations.literal: Three sons: Bin, Hong, and Fan.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Bin, Hong, and Fan.

translations.literal: Bin, styled Shuda, was recommended as Worthy and Able but declined to take office.
translations.idiomatic: Bin, styled Shuda, was recommended as Worthy and Able but refused appointment.

translations.literal: Two sons: Xi and Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Xi and Chong.

translations.literal: Chong, styled Bokuo, aide to the Minister of Works; he bore Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, styled Bokuo, served as an aide to the Minister of Works; his son was Ji.

sentences.zh: 畿字伯侯，魏河東太守、豐樂戴侯。

translations.literal: Ji, styled Bohou, Governor of Hedong in Wei, Marquis Dai of Fengle.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, styled Bohou, served Wei as Governor of Hedong and held the title Marquis Dai of Fengle.

translations.literal: Three sons: Shu, Li, and Kuan.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Shu, Li, and Kuan.

sentences.zh: 恕字伯務，弘農太守、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: Shu, styled Bowu, Governor of Hongnong and Governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, styled Bowu, served as Governor of Hongnong and Governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 生預，字元凱，晉荊州刺史、征南大將軍、當陽侯。

translations.literal: He bore Yu, styled Yuankai, Governor of Jingzhou of Jin, General Who Campaigns South, Marquis of Dangyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yu, styled Yuankai, who served Jin as Governor of Jingzhou and General Who Campaigns South and held the title Marquis of Dangyang.

translations.literal: Four sons: Xi, Ji, Dan, and Yin.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Xi, Ji, Dan, and Yin.

translations.literal: Xi, styled Shijia, served as Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, styled Shijia, served as Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.

translations.literal: Great-grandson Ti.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson was Ti.

translations.literal: Two sons: Chu and Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Chu and Xiu.

translations.literal: Xiu had two sons: Guo and Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu had two sons: Guo and Jiao.

sentences.zh: 皎生徽，徽字曄，隋懷州長史、豐鄉侯。

translations.literal: Jiao bore Hui; Hui, styled Ye, was Senior Administrator of Huaizhou in Sui, Marquis of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao's son was Hui, styled Ye, who served Sui as Senior Administrator of Huaizhou and held the title Marquis of Fengxiang.

translations.literal: He bore Tuo and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Tuo and Yan.

sentences.zh: 京兆杜氏：漢建平侯延年二十世孫文、瑤，與義興公杲同房。

translations.literal: The Jingzhao Du clan: Wen and Yao, twentieth-generation descendants of Marquis Jianping Yannian of Han, were of the same house as Duke of Yixing, Gao.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingzhao Du clan: Wen and Yao, twentieth-generation descendants of Marquis Jianping Yannian of Han, belonged to the same house as Duke of Yixing, Gao.

sentences.zh: 襄陽杜氏出自當陽侯預少子尹，字世甫，晉弘農太守。

translations.literal: The Xiangyang Du clan was traced to Yin, youngest son of Marquis of Dangyang Yu, styled Shifu, Governor of Hongnong under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiangyang Du clan descended from Yin, youngest son of Marquis of Dangyang Yu, styled Shifu, who served Jin as Governor of Hongnong.

translations.literal: Two sons: Can and Bi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Can and Bi.

translations.literal: Can, styled Honggu, Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: Can, styled Honggu, served as Attendant at Court.

translations.literal: He bore Xi, styled Zusi, Governor of Shangluo.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xi, styled Zusi, Governor of Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 襲生摽，摽字文湛，中書侍郎、池陽侯。

translations.literal: Xi bore Biao; Biao, styled Wenzhan, Vice Director of the Secretariat, Marquis of Chiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's son was Biao, styled Wenzhan, who served as Vice Director of the Secretariat and held the title Marquis of Chiyang.

sentences.zh: 生沖，字方進，中書侍郎，襲池陽侯。

translations.literal: He bore Chong, styled Fangjin, Vice Director of the Secretariat; he inherited the marquisate of Chiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Chong, styled Fangjin, Vice Director of the Secretariat, who inherited the marquisate of Chiyang.

sentences.zh: 生洪泰，字道廓，南徐州刺史，襲池陽侯。

translations.literal: He bore Hongtai, styled Daokuo, Governor of Southern Xuzhou; he inherited the marquisate of Chiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Hongtai, styled Daokuo, Governor of Southern Xuzhou, who also inherited the marquisate of Chiyang.

translations.literal: Two sons: Zuyue and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Zuyue and Yong.

sentences.zh: 洹水杜氏出自戴侯恕少子寬，字務叔，孝廉，郎中。

translations.literal: The Huanshui Du clan was traced to Kuan, youngest son of Marquis Dai Shu, styled Wushu, Filial and Incorrupt graduate, Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Huanshui Du clan descended from Kuan, youngest son of Marquis Dai Shu, styled Wushu, a Filial and Incorrupt graduate who served as Gentleman of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 曾孫曼，仕石趙，從事中郎、河東太守。

translations.literal: Great-grandson Man served the Later Zhao of the Shi clan as Attendant Gentleman and Governor of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Man served Later Zhao as Attendant Gentleman and Governor of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 初居鄴，葬父洹水，後亦徙居洹水。

translations.literal: At first they resided at Ye; they buried his father at Huanshui, and later also moved to live at Huanshui.
translations.idiomatic: At first the family lived at Ye; after burying his father at Huanshui, they later moved there as well.

sentences.zh: 五世孫君賜，君賜生景、宣明。

translations.literal: Fifth-generation descendant Junsi; Junsi bore Jing and Xuanming.
translations.idiomatic: A fifth-generation descendant was Junsi, who had two sons, Jing and Xuanming.

translations.literal: Jing bore Ziyu.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's son was Ziyu.

sentences.zh: 濮陽杜氏出自赫子威，世居濮陽，裔孫模，後魏濮陽太守，因家焉。

translations.literal: The Puyang Du clan was traced to Wei, son of He; they had long resided at Puyang. Collateral descendant Mo served as Governor of Puyang under Later Wei and made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: The Puyang Du clan descended from Wei, son of He, and had long lived at Puyang. A collateral descendant, Mo, served Later Wei as Governor of Puyang and established the family there.

translations.literal: Mo bore Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Mo's son was Liang.

translations.literal: Of the Du clan, eleven chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Du clan produced eleven chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 如晦、淹、元穎、審權、讓能、黃裳、佑、悰、正倫、鴻漸、暹。

translations.literal: Ruhui, Yan, Yuanying, Shenquan, Rangneng, Huangchang, You, Cong, Zhenglun, Hongjian, and Xian.
translations.idiomatic: They were Ruhui, Yan, Yuanying, Shenquan, Rangneng, Huangchang, You, Cong, Zhenglun, Hongjian, and Xian.

sentences.zh: 李隴西李氏李氏武陽房出自興聖皇帝第七子豫，其後為武陽房。

translations.literal: The Wuyang branch of the Longxi Li clan of the Li surname was traced to Yu, seventh son of the Emperor of Exalted Sagacity; his descendants formed the Wuyang branch.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuyang branch of the Longxi Li clan descended from Yu, seventh son of the Emperor of Exalted Sagacity; his descendants became the Wuyang branch.

sentences.zh: 姑臧大房出自興聖皇帝第八子飜，字士舉，東晉祁連、酒泉、晉昌太守。

translations.literal: The major Gugu branch was traced to Fan, eighth son of the Emperor of Exalted Sagacity, styled Shiju, Governor of Qilian, Jiuquan, and Jinchang under Eastern Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The major Gugu branch descended from Fan, eighth son of the Emperor of Exalted Sagacity, styled Shiju, who served Eastern Jin as Governor of Qilian, Jiuquan, and Jinchang.

translations.literal: Three sons: Bao, Huaida, and Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Bao, Huaida, and Kang.

translations.literal: Kang, Governor of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: Kang served as Governor of Donglai.

sentences.zh: 生思穆，字叔仁，後魏營州刺史、樂平宣惠伯。

translations.literal: He bore Simu, styled Shuren, Governor of Yingzhou under Later Wei, Baron Xuanhui of Leping.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Simu, styled Shuren, who served Later Wei as Governor of Yingzhou and held the title Baron Xuanhui of Leping.

sentences.zh: 生奬，字道休，北齊魏尹、廣平侯。

translations.literal: He bore Jiang, styled Daoxiu, Intendant of Wei under Northern Qi, Marquis of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jiang, styled Daoxiu, who served Northern Qi as Intendant of Wei and held the title Marquis of Guangping.

translations.literal: He bore Gui, Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Gui, a Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 生斌，散騎侍郎，襲樂平伯。

translations.literal: He bore Bin, Attendant Gentleman of the Dispersed Cavalry; he inherited the barony of Leping.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Bin, Attendant Gentleman of the Dispersed Cavalry, who inherited the barony of Leping.

sentences.zh: 寶七子：承、茂、輔、佐、公業、沖、仁宗。

translations.literal: Bao had seven sons: Cheng, Mao, Fu, Zuo, Gongye, Chong, and Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: Bao had seven sons: Cheng, Mao, Fu, Zuo, Gongye, Chong, and Renzong.

translations.literal: Cheng was styled the Gugu branch.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng founded the Gugu branch.

sentences.zh: 丹楊房：晉東莞太守雍長子曰倫，五世孫文度，西涼安定太守，與族人寶入後魏，因居京兆山北。

translations.literal: The Danyang branch: Yong of Jin, Governor of Dongguan—his eldest son was Lun; fifth-generation descendant Wendu, Governor of Anding under Western Liang, entered Later Wei together with his clansman Bao and thus settled north of the mountains in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The Danyang branch: Yong of Jin served as Governor of Dongguan, and his eldest son was Lun. A fifth-generation descendant, Wendu, Governor of Anding under Western Liang, entered Later Wei together with his clansman Bao and settled north of the mountains in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 漢騎都尉陵降匈奴，裔孫歸魏，見於丙殿，賜氏曰丙。

translations.literal: Han Cavalry Commandant Ling surrendered to the Xiongnu; a collateral descendant returned to Wei, appeared in the Hall of Bing, and was granted the surname Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Han Cavalry Commandant Ling surrendered to the Xiongnu; a collateral descendant later returned to Wei, was received in the Hall of Bing, and was granted the surname Bing.

sentences.zh: 後周有信州總管龍居縣公明，明生粲，唐左監門大將軍、應國公，高祖與之有舊，以避世祖名，賜姓李氏。

translations.literal: Later Zhou had Commandant-in-Chief of Xinzhou, Duke of Longju County, Ming; Ming bore Can, Left Gate Guardian Grand General of Tang, Duke of Ying; Gaozu had old ties with him and, to avoid the name of Shizu, granted him the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou had Ming, Commandant-in-Chief of Xinzhou and Duke of Longju County; Ming's son was Can, Left Gate Guardian Grand General of Tang and Duke of Ying. Gaozu had old ties with him and, to avoid the personal name of Shizu, granted him the surname Li.

translations.literal: The Longxi Li clan later moved to Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The Longxi Li clan later relocated to Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 隴西李氏定著四房：其一曰武陽，二曰姑臧，三曰燉煌，四曰丹楊。

translations.literal: The Longxi Li clan had four established branches: the first called Wuyang, the second Gugu, the third Dunhuang, and the fourth Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Longxi Li clan was divided into four established branches: Wuyang, Gugu, Dunhuang, and Danyang.

translations.literal: Ten chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: They produced ten chief ministers.

translations.literal: The Wuyang branch had Jiongxiu;
translations.idiomatic: The Wuyang branch included Jiongxiu;

sentences.zh: 姑臧大房有義琰、蔚、揆、逢吉；

translations.literal: The major Gugu branch had Yiyan, Wei, Kui, and Fengji;
translations.idiomatic: The major Gugu branch included Yiyan, Wei, Kui, and Fengji;

translations.literal: The Danyang branch had Jing and Zhaode;
translations.idiomatic: The Danyang branch included Jing and Zhaode;

translations.literal: There were also Daoguang, Yuanhong, and Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Daoguang, Yuanhong, and Sheng.

sentences.zh: 趙郡李氏趙郡李氏，出自秦司徒曇次子璣，字伯衡，秦太傅。

translations.literal: The Zhao Commandery Li clan of the Zhao Commandery Li surname was traced to Ji, second son of Minister over the Masses Tan of Qin, styled Boheng, Grand Tutor of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao Commandery Li clan descended from Ji, second son of Qin Minister over the Masses Tan, styled Boheng, who served as Grand Tutor of Qin.

translations.literal: Three sons: Yun, Mu, and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Yun, Mu, and Qi.

sentences.zh: 牧為趙相，封武安君，始居趙郡。

translations.literal: Mu served as Chancellor of Zhao, was enfeoffed as Lord of Wu'an, and first settled in Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Mu served as Chancellor of Zhao, was enfeoffed as Lord of Wu'an, and first established the family in Zhao Commandery.

translations.literal: Between Zhao Na and Dun Ruo, Mu was killed.
translations.idiomatic: During the conflict between Zhao Na and Dun Ruo, Mu was killed.

sentences.zh: 齊為中山相，亦家焉，即中山始祖也。

translations.literal: Qi served as Chancellor of Zhongshan and also made his home there; he was the founding ancestor of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Qi served as Chancellor of Zhongshan and also settled there; he was the founding ancestor of the Zhongshan line.

translations.literal: Mu had three sons: Mi, Hong, and Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Mu had three sons: Mi, Hong, and Xian.

sentences.zh: 汨，秦中大夫、詹事，生諒、左車、仲車。

translations.literal: Mi, Palace Grandee and Household Master of Qin; he bore Liang, Zuoche, and Zhongche.
translations.idiomatic: Mi served Qin as Palace Grandee and Household Master; his sons were Liang, Zuoche, and Zhongche.

sentences.zh: 左車，趙廣武君，生常、伯、遐。

translations.literal: Zuoche, Lord of Guangwu of Zhao; he bore Chang, Bo, and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Zuoche held the title Lord of Guangwu of Zhao; his sons were Chang, Bo, and Xia.

sentences.zh: 遐字伯友，漢涿郡守，生岳、德、文、班。

translations.literal: Xia, styled Boyou, Administrator of Zhuo Commandery of Han; he bore Yue, De, Wen, and Ban.
translations.idiomatic: Xia, styled Boyou, served Han as Administrator of Zhuo Commandery; his sons were Yue, De, Wen, and Ban.

sentences.zh: 岳字長卿，諫議大夫，生秉、義。

translations.literal: Yue, styled Changqing, Remonstrance and Discussion Grand Master; he bore Bing and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, styled Changqing, served as Remonstrance and Discussion Grand Master; his sons were Bing and Yi.

sentences.zh: 秉字世範，潁川太守，因徙家焉。

translations.literal: Bing, styled Shifan, Administrator of Yingchuan Commandery; thereupon he moved his household there.
translations.idiomatic: Bing, styled Shifan, served as Administrator of Yingchuan Commandery and thereupon moved his household there.

translations.literal: He bore Yi, Xie, and Min.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yi, Xie, and Min.

sentences.zh: 敏，五大夫將軍，生謨、道、朗。

translations.literal: Min, General of the Five Grand Masters; he bore Mo, Dao, and Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Min served as General of the Five Grandees; his sons were Mo, Dao, and Lang.

sentences.zh: 謨字道謀，臨淮太守，生哆、華、旭。

translations.literal: Mo, styled Daomou, Administrator of Linhuai Commandery; he bore Duo, Hua, and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Mo, styled Daomou, served as Administrator of Linhuai Commandery; his sons were Duo, Hua, and Xu.

sentences.zh: 哆字子讓，上黨太守，生護、元。

translations.literal: Duo, styled Zirang, Administrator of Shangdang Commandery; he bore Hu and Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Duo, styled Zirang, served as Administrator of Shangdang Commandery; his sons were Hu and Yuan.

sentences.zh: 護字鴻默，酒泉太守，生武、昭、奮。

translations.literal: Hu, styled Hongmo, Administrator of Jiuquan Commandery; he bore Wu, Zhao, and Fen.
translations.idiomatic: Hu, styled Hongmo, served as Administrator of Jiuquan Commandery; his sons were Wu, Zhao, and Fen.

sentences.zh: 武字昭先，東郡太守、太常卿，生讚、脩、弈、就。

translations.literal: Wu, styled Zhaoxian, Administrator of Dong Commandery and Minister of Ceremonies; he bore Zan, Xiu, Yi, and Jiu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, styled Zhaoxian, served as Administrator of Dong Commandery and Minister of Ceremonies; his sons were Zan, Xiu, Yi, and Jiu.

sentences.zh: 脩字伯游，後漢太尉，生諒、叔、訓、季。

translations.literal: Xiu, styled Boyou, Grand Commandant of Later Han; he bore Liang, Shu, Xun, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu, styled Boyou, served Later Han as Grand Commandant; his sons were Liang, Shu, Xun, and Ji.

translations.literal: Liang, styled Shiyi, Chancellor of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Liang, styled Shiyi, served as Chancellor of Zhao.

translations.literal: He bore Ying, styled Yuanli, Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Ying, styled Yuanli, who served as Intendant of Henan.

translations.literal: He bore Gui, Zan, and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Gui, Zan, and Jin.

sentences.zh: 瑾字叔瑜，東平相，避難復居趙，生志、恢、宣。

translations.literal: Jin, styled Shuyu, Chancellor of Dongping; fleeing turmoil he again settled in Zhao; he bore Zhi, Hui, and Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, styled Shuyu, served as Chancellor of Dongping; fleeing turmoil he returned to settle in Zhao; his sons were Zhi, Hui, and Xuan.

translations.literal: Hui, styled Shuxing; he bore Ding, Tai, Jiang, and Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, styled Shuxing, had sons Ding, Tai, Jiang, and Shuo.

sentences.zh: 定字文義，魏水衡都尉、漁陽太守，生伯括、機、叔括、季括。

translations.literal: Ding, styled Wenyi, Chief Commandant of Waterworks of Wei and Administrator of Yuyang Commandery; he bore Bokuo, Ji, Shukuo, and Jikuo.
translations.idiomatic: Ding, styled Wenyi, served Wei as Chief Commandant of Waterworks and Administrator of Yuyang Commandery; his sons were Bokuo, Ji, Shukuo, and Jikuo.

sentences.zh: 機字仲括，太學博士、臨江樂安二郡太守，生羣、瓌、密、楷、越。

translations.literal: Ji, styled Zhongkuo, Erudite of the Imperial Academy and Administrator of the two commanderies of Linjiang and Le'an; he bore Qun, Gui, Mi, Kai, and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, styled Zhongkuo, served as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and Administrator of both Linjiang and Le'an commanderies; his sons were Qun, Gui, Mi, Kai, and Yue.

sentences.zh: 楷字雄方，晉司農丞、治書侍御史，避趙王倫之難，徙居常山。

translations.literal: Kai, styled Xiongfang, Assistant Minister of Agriculture of Jin and Secretary-Draft Attendant Censor; fleeing the disaster of Prince of Zhao Lun, he moved to Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Kai, styled Xiongfang, served Jin as Assistant Minister of Agriculture and Secretary-Draft Attendant Censor; fleeing the upheaval of Prince of Zhao Lun, he moved his household to Changshan.

translations.literal: Five sons: Ji, Huang, Fen, Jin, and Rui.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Ji, Huang, Fen, Jin, and Rui.

translations.literal: Rui's son Xu—the brothers lived at the east of the lane;
translations.idiomatic: Rui's son Xu and his brothers lived on the east side of the lane;

translations.literal: Jin's son Sheng—the brothers lived at the west of the lane.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's son Sheng and his brothers lived on the west side of the lane.

sentences.zh: 故叡為東祖，芬與弟勁共稱西祖，輯與弟晃共稱南祖。

translations.literal: Therefore Rui was made the Eastern Branch; Fen together with his younger brother Jin were jointly called the Western Branch; Ji together with his younger brother Huang were jointly called the Southern Branch.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly Rui was designated the Eastern Branch; Fen and his younger brother Jin together were called the Western Branch; and Ji and his younger brother Huang together were called the Southern Branch.

sentences.zh: 自楷徙居平棘南，通號平棘李氏。

translations.literal: From Kai's removal to south of Pingji, they were commonly styled the Pingji Li clan.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Kai moved south of Pingji, the line was commonly known as the Pingji Li clan.

sentences.zh: 輯字護宗，高密太守，子慎敦，居柏仁，子孫甚微，與晃南徙故壘，故輯、晃皆稱南祖。

translations.literal: Ji, styled Huzong, Administrator of Gaomi Commandery; his son Shendun settled at Boren—the descendants were very few; together with Huang he moved south to Gulei; therefore both Ji and Huang were called the Southern Branch.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, styled Huzong, served as Administrator of Gaomi Commandery; his son Shendun settled at Boren, but the descendants were very few; Ji and Huang moved south together to Gulei, and therefore both Ji and Huang were called the Southern Branch.

translations.literal: Huang, styled Zhonghuang, Chief Clerk of the Southern Defense Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Huang, styled Zhonghuang, served as Chief Clerk of the Southern Defense Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 生羲，字敬仲，燕司空長史。

translations.literal: He bore Xi, styled Jingzhong, Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xi, styled Jingzhong, who served as Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works of Yan.

translations.literal: He bore Ji, styled Yantong, Attendant of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Ji, styled Yantong, who served as Attendant of the Eastern Palace.

translations.literal: He bore Cong, styled Xiaoshi, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Cong, styled Xiaoshi, who served as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

translations.literal: Two sons: Zhen and Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Zhen and Rong.

sentences.zh: 羲之後有萬安，自趙郡徙于管城。

translations.literal: After Xi there was Wan'an, who moved from Zhao Commandery to Guancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Among Xi's descendants was Wan'an, who moved from Zhao Commandery to Guancheng.

sentences.zh: 南祖之後有善權，後魏譙郡太守，徙居譙。

translations.literal: Among descendants of the Southern Branch was Shanquan, Administrator of Qiao Commandery of Later Wei; he moved to Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Southern Branch's descendants was Shanquan, who served Later Wei as Administrator of Qiao Commandery and moved his household to Qiao.

sentences.zh: 生延觀，徐梁二州刺史，生續。

translations.literal: He bore Yangguan, Inspector of Xu and Liang provinces; he bore Xu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yangguan, who served as Inspector of Xu and Liang provinces; Yangguan's son was Xu.

sentences.zh: 東祖叡，字幼黃，高平太守、江陵寧公。

translations.literal: The Eastern Branch [ancestor] Rui, styled Youhuang, Administrator of Gaoping Commandery and Duke Ning of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Branch ancestor Rui, styled Youhuang, served as Administrator of Gaoping Commandery and Duke Ning of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 生勗，字景賢，頓丘太守、大中正。

translations.literal: He bore Xu, styled Jingxian, Administrator of Dunqiu Commandery and Chief Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xu, styled Jingxian, who served as Administrator of Dunqiu Commandery and Chief Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 生頤，字彥祖，高陽太守、武安公。

translations.literal: He bore Yi, styled Yanzu, Administrator of Gaoyang Commandery and Duke of Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yi, styled Yanzu, who served as Administrator of Gaoyang Commandery and Duke of Wu'an.

translations.literal: Four sons: Xie, Xi, Feng, and Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Xie, Xi, Feng, and Zeng.

translations.literal: Among descendants of the Eastern Branch there was also E.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Eastern Branch's descendants there was also E.

sentences.zh: 西祖勁字少黃，晉治書侍御史。

translations.literal: The Western Branch [ancestor] Jin, styled Shaohuang, Secretary-Draft Attendant Censor of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Branch ancestor Jin, styled Shaohuang, served Jin as Secretary-Draft Attendant Censor.

translations.literal: Two sons: Sheng and Long.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Sheng and Long.

sentences.zh: 遼東李氏：璣少子齊，趙相，初居中山，十三世孫寶，字君長，後漢玄菟都尉，徙襄平。

translations.literal: Liaodong Li clan: Qi, youngest son of Ji, Chancellor of Zhao; at first he dwelt in Zhongshan. In the thirteenth generation, his descendant Bao, styled Junchang, Colonel of Xuantu of Later Han, moved to Xiangping.
translations.idiomatic: The Liaodong Li clan: Qi, youngest son of Ji, served as Chancellor of Zhao and first settled in Zhongshan. In the thirteenth generation, his descendant Bao, styled Junchang, served Later Han as Colonel of Xuantu and moved to Xiangping.

translations.literal: He bore Xiong, Chief Clerk of the Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xiong, who served as Chief Clerk of the Chariots and Cavalry.

translations.literal: He bore Liang, styled Weiming, Magistrate of Yuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Liang, styled Weiming, who served as Magistrate of Yuanwu.

translations.literal: He bore Min, Administrator of Henei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Min, who served as Administrator of Henei Commandery.

translations.literal: He bore Xin.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xin.

sentences.zh: 生胤，字宣伯，晉司徒、廣陸成侯。

translations.literal: He bore Yin, styled Xuanbo, Minister over the Masses of Jin and Marquis Cheng of Guanglu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yin, styled Xuanbo, who served Jin as Minister over the Masses and held the title Marquis Cheng of Guanglu.

translations.literal: He bore Gu, styled Wanji, Attendant Cavalryman-at-Large.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Gu, styled Wanji, who served as Attendant Cavalryman-at-Large.

sentences.zh: 生志，字彥道，陽平太守、嗣廣陸侯。

translations.literal: He bore Zhi, styled Yandao, Administrator of Yangping Commandery and heir to the Marquis of Guanglu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhi, styled Yandao, who served as Administrator of Yangping Commandery and succeeded to the title Marquis of Guanglu.

translations.literal: Younger brother Chen; Chen's grandson Gen.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Chen; Chen's grandson was Gen.

sentences.zh: 江夏李氏：漢酒泉太守護次子昭，昭少子就，後漢會稽太守、高陽侯，徙居江夏平春。

translations.literal: Jiangxia Li clan: Zhao, second son of Hu, Administrator of Jiuquan of Han—Zhao's youngest son Jiu, Administrator of Kuaiji Commandery of Later Han and Marquis of Gaoyang, moved to Pingchun in Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangxia Li clan: Zhao, second son of Hu, Administrator of Jiuquan under Han; Jiu, Zhao's youngest son, served Later Han as Administrator of Kuaiji Commandery and Marquis of Gaoyang, and moved his household to Pingchun in Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 六世孫式，字景則，東晉侍中。

translations.literal: In the sixth generation, his descendant Shi, styled Jingze, Attendant-in-Ordinary of Eastern Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth generation, his descendant Shi, styled Jingze, served Eastern Jin as Attendant-in-Ordinary.

translations.literal: He bore Ni.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Ni.

translations.literal: Ni bore Shang, styled Maozhong.
translations.idiomatic: Ni's son was Shang, styled Maozhong.

translations.literal: He bore Ju, styled Maoyue, Inspector of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Ju, styled Maoyue, who served as Inspector of Jiang Province.

translations.literal: He bore Chong, styled Hongdu, Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Chong, styled Hongdu, who served as Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 生顒，郡舉孝廉，七世孫元哲。

translations.literal: He bore Yong; the commandery recommended him as Filial and Incorrupt. In the seventh generation [descended] Yuanzhe.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yong, whom the commandery recommended as Filial and Incorrupt; in the seventh generation descended Yuanzhe.

sentences.zh: 漢中李氏：漢東郡太守、太常卿武孫頡，後漢博士，始居漢中南鄭。

translations.literal: Hanzhong Li clan: Jie, grandson of Wu, Administrator of Dong Commandery and Minister of Ceremonies of Han, Erudite of Later Han; first settled in Nanzheng in Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanzhong Li clan: Jie, grandson of Wu, Administrator of Dong Commandery and Minister of Ceremonies under Han, served Later Han as Erudite and first settled in Nanzheng in Hanzhong.

translations.literal: He bore He, styled Mengjie, Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: His son was He, styled Mengjie, who served as Minister over the Masses.

translations.literal: He bore Gu, styled Zijian, Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Gu, styled Zijian, who served as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 生三子：基字憲公，茲字季公，爕字德公，安平相。

translations.literal: He bore three sons: Ji, styled Xiangong; Ci, styled Jigong; and Ye, styled Degong, Chancellor of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Ji, styled Xiangong; Ci, styled Jigong; and Ye, styled Degong, who served as Chancellor of Anping.

translations.literal: In the twelfth generation [descended] Delin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth generation descended Delin.

sentences.zh: 趙郡李氏定著六房：其一曰南祖，二曰東祖，三曰西祖，四曰遼東，五曰江夏，六曰漢中。

translations.literal: The Zhao Commandery Li clan was definitively established in six branches: the first was called the Southern Branch, the second the Eastern Branch, the third the Western Branch, the fourth Liaodong, the fifth Jiangxia, and the sixth Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao Commandery Li clan was definitively divided into six branches: the Southern Branch, the Eastern Branch, the Western Branch, Liaodong, Jiangxia, and Hanzhong.

translations.literal: Seventeen chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: There were seventeen chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 南祖有游道、藩、固言、日知、敬玄、紳、元素；

translations.literal: The Southern Branch had Youdao, Fan, Guy, Rizhi, Jingxuan, Shen, and Yuansu;
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Branch produced Youdao, Fan, Guy, Rizhi, Jingxuan, Shen, and Yuansu;

translations.literal: The Eastern Branch had Jiang, Qiao, and Jue;
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Branch produced Jiang, Qiao, and Jue;

translations.literal: The Western Branch had Huaiyuan, Jifu, and Deyu;
translations.idiomatic: The Western Branch produced Huaiyuan, Jifu, and Deyu;

translations.literal: Liaodong had Bi;
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong produced Bi;

translations.literal: Jiangxia had Yong and Xi;
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxia produced Yong and Xi;

translations.literal: Hanzhong had Anqi.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhong produced Anqi.

translations.literal: The Wang clan of the Wang surname was traced to the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Wang clan descended from the Ji surname.

sentences.zh: 周靈王太子晉以直諫廢為庶人，其子宗敬為司徒，時人號曰「王家」，因以為氏。

translations.literal: Prince Jin, crown prince of King Ling of Zhou, was deposed to commoner status for his blunt remonstrance; his son Zongjing served as Minister over the Masses, and people of the time called them the "Wang family," hence they took it as their surname.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin, crown prince of King Ling of Zhou, was demoted to commoner status for his blunt remonstrance; his son Zongjing served as Minister over the Masses, and people of the time called them the "Wang family," from which they took their surname.

translations.literal: In the eighth generation, his descendant Cuo served as a general of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth generation, his descendant Cuo served as a general of Wei.

translations.literal: He bore Ben, who served as Palace Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Ben, who served as Palace Grandee.

translations.literal: Ben bore Yu, who served as Senior General.
translations.idiomatic: Ben's son was Yu, who served as Senior General.

translations.literal: Yu bore Xi, who served as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's son was Xi, who served as Minister of Works.

translations.literal: Xi bore Hui, enfeoffed as Lord of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's son was Hui, who was enfeoffed as Lord of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 生元，元生頤，皆以中大夫召，不就。

translations.literal: He bore Yuan; Yuan bore Yi—both were summoned as Palace Grandees and declined.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Yuan, and Yuan had a son Yi; both were summoned to serve as Palace Grandees and declined.

translations.literal: He bore Jian, Grand General of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jian, who served Qin as Grand General.

translations.literal: He bore Ben, styled Dian, Marquis of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Ben, styled Dian, who held the title Marquis of Wuling.

translations.literal: He bore Li, styled Ming, Marquis of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Li, styled Ming, who held the title Marquis of Wucheng.

translations.literal: Two sons: Yuan and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Yuan and Wei.

sentences.zh: 元避秦亂，遷于琅邪，後徙臨沂。

translations.literal: Yuan, fleeing the turmoil of Qin, moved to Langya; later [the family] relocated to Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, fleeing the chaos of Qin, moved to Langya; later the family relocated to Linyi.

sentences.zh: 四世孫吉，字子陽，漢諫大夫，始家皐虞，後徙臨沂都鄉南仁里。

translations.literal: In the fourth generation, his descendant Ji, styled Ziyang, Remonstrance and Criticism Grand Master of Han, first made his home at Gaoyu; later he moved to Nanren Lane, Ducal Village, Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth generation, his descendant Ji, styled Ziyang, served Han as Remonstrance and Criticism Grand Master, first establishing the family at Gaoyu and later moving to Nanren Lane in Ducal Village, Linyi.

translations.literal: He bore Jun, styled Weishan, Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jun, styled Weishan, who served as Grand Censor.

translations.literal: Two sons: Chong and You.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Chong and You.

sentences.zh: 崇字德禮，大司空、扶平侯。

translations.literal: Chong, styled Deli, Grand Minister of Works and Marquis of Fuping.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, styled Deli, served as Grand Minister of Works and held the title Marquis of Fuping.

sentences.zh: 生遵，字伯業，後漢中大夫、義鄉侯。

translations.literal: He bore Zun, styled Boye, Palace Grandee of Later Han and Marquis of Yixiang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zun, styled Boye, who served Later Han as Palace Grandee and held the title Marquis of Yixiang.

translations.literal: He bore two sons: Shi and Yin.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Shi and Yin.

translations.literal: Yin, styled Shaoxuan, Clerk to the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, styled Shaoxuan, served as Clerk to the Grand General.

translations.literal: Four sons: Yi, Rui, Dian, and Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Yi, Rui, Dian, and Rong.

translations.literal: Rong, styled Juwei.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was styled Juwei.

translations.literal: Two sons: Xiang and Lan.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Xiang and Lan.

sentences.zh: 覽字玄通，晉宗正卿、即丘貞子。

translations.literal: Lan, styled Xuantong, Director of the Imperial Clan of Jin and Viscount Zhen of Jiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Lan, styled Xuantong, served Jin as Director of the Imperial Clan and held the title Viscount Zhen of Jiqiu.

translations.literal: Six sons: Zai, Ji, Hui, Zheng, Yan, and Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: Zai, Ji, Hui, Zheng, Yan, and Chen.

sentences.zh: 栽字士初，撫軍長史，襲即丘子。

translations.literal: Zai, styled Shichu, Chief Clerk of the Pacification Army; he inherited the viscounty of Jiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zai, styled Shichu, served as Chief Clerk of the Pacification Army and inherited the viscounty of Jiqiu.

translations.literal: Three sons: Dao, Ying, and Chang.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Dao, Ying, and Chang.

sentences.zh: 導字茂弘，丞相始興文獻公。

translations.literal: Dao, styled Maohong, Chancellor and Duke Wenxian of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Dao, styled Maohong, served as Chancellor and held the title Duke Wenxian of Shixing.

translations.literal: Six sons: Yue, Tian, Shao, Qia, Xie, and Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: Yue, Tian, Shao, Qia, Xie, and Hui.

translations.literal: Qia, styled Jinghe, Attendant Cavalryman-at-Large.
translations.idiomatic: Qia, styled Jinghe, served as Attendant Cavalryman-at-Large.

translations.literal: Two sons: Xun and Min.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Xun and Min.

sentences.zh: 珣字元琳，尚書令、前將軍，謚曰獻穆。

translations.literal: Xun, styled Yuanlin, Director of the Masters of Writing and General of the Vanguard; his posthumous title was Xianmu.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, styled Yuanlin, served as Director of the Masters of Writing and General of the Vanguard; his posthumous title was Xianmu.

translations.literal: Five sons: Hong, Yu, Liu, Ru, and Tanshou.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Hong, Yu, Liu, Ru, and Tanshou.

sentences.zh: 曇首，宋侍中、太子詹事、豫寧文侯。

translations.literal: Tanshou, Attendant-in-Ordinary of Song, Grand Master of the Heir Apparent, and Marquis Wen of Yunin.
translations.idiomatic: Tanshou served Song as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Master of the Heir Apparent, and held the title Marquis Wen of Yunin.

translations.literal: Two sons: Sengchuo and Sengqian.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Sengchuo and Sengqian.

sentences.zh: 僧綽，中書侍郎，襲豫寧愍侯。

translations.literal: Sengchuo, Vice Director of the Secretariat; he inherited the marquisate of Min of Yunin.
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo served as Vice Director of the Secretariat and inherited the title Marquis Min of Yunin.

sentences.zh: 生儉，字仲寶，齊侍中、尚書令、南昌文憲公。

translations.literal: He bore Jian, styled Zhongbao, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Masters of Writing of Qi, Duke Wenxian of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jian, styled Zhongbao, who served Qi as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Masters of Writing and held the title Duke Wenxian of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 生騫，字思寂，梁給事中、南昌安侯。

translations.literal: He bore Qian, styled Siji, Attendant at the Gate of Liang and Marquis An of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Qian, styled Siji, who served Liang as Attendant at the Gate and held the title Marquis An of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 生規，字威明，左戶尚書、南昌章侯。

translations.literal: He bore Gui, styled Weiming, Left Minister of the Household and Marquis Zhang of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Gui, styled Weiming, who served as Left Minister of the Household and held the title Marquis Zhang of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 生褒，褒字子淵，後周光祿大夫、石泉康侯。

translations.literal: He bore Bao; Bao was styled Ziyuan, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness of Later Zhou and Marquis Kang of Shiquan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Bao, styled Ziyuan, who served Later Zhou as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and held the title Marquis Kang of Shiquan.

sentences.zh: 生鼒，字玉鉉，隋安都通守、石泉明威侯。

translations.literal: He bore Zi, styled Yuxuan, General Administrator of Andu of Sui and Marquis Mingwei of Shiquan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zi, styled Yuxuan, who served Sui as General Administrator of Andu and held the title Marquis Mingwei of Shiquan.

translations.literal: Sons: Hongrang and Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Hongrang and Hongzhi.

translations.literal: Zheng, styled Shize, Lang of the Masters of Writing of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng, styled Shize, served Jin as a Lang of the Masters of Writing.

translations.literal: Three sons: Yi, Kuang, and Bin.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Yi, Kuang, and Bin.

sentences.zh: 彬字世儒，尚書右僕射、肅侯。

translations.literal: Bin, styled Shiru, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Marquis Su.
translations.idiomatic: Bin, styled Shiru, served as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and held the title Marquis Su.

translations.literal: Two sons: Pengzhi and Biaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Pengzhi and Biaozhi.

sentences.zh: 彪之字叔武，尚書令，謚曰簡。

translations.literal: Biaozhi, styled Shuwu, Director of the Masters of Writing; his posthumous title was Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Biaozhi, styled Shuwu, served as Director of the Masters of Writing; his posthumous title was Jian.

translations.literal: Two sons: Yuezhi and Linzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Yuezhi and Linzhi.

sentences.zh: 臨之生納之，皆御史中丞。

translations.literal: Linzhi bore Nazhi; both served as Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Linzhi's son was Nazhi; both Linzhi and Nazhi served as Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 納之生准之，字元魯，宋丹楊尹。

translations.literal: Nazhi bore Zhunzhi, styled Yuanlu, Administrator of Danyang of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Nazhi's son was Zhunzhi, styled Yuanlu, who served Song as Administrator of Danyang.

translations.literal: He bore Yuzhi, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yuzhi, who served as General Who Pacifies the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 生進之，梁左衛將軍、建寧公。

translations.literal: He bore Jinzhi, Left Guards General of Liang and Duke of Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jinzhi, who served Liang as Left Guards General and held the title Duke of Jianning.

translations.literal: He bore Qing, General Who Pacifies the South and Duke of Zhonglu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Qing, who served as General Who Pacifies the South and held the title Duke of Zhonglu.

translations.literal: He bore Meng.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Meng.

sentences.zh: 太原王氏出自離次子威，漢揚州刺史，九世孫霸，字儒仲，居太原晉陽，後漢連聘不至。

translations.literal: The Taiyuan Wang clan was traced to Li's second son Wei, Governor of Yang Province of Han; in the ninth generation, his descendant Ba, styled Ruzhong, dwelt at Jinyang in Taiyuan and repeatedly declined summons under Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiyuan Wang clan descended from Li's second son Wei, who served Han as Governor of Yang Province; in the ninth generation, his descendant Ba, styled Ruzhong, settled at Jinyang in Taiyuan and repeatedly declined Later Han summons to office.

sentences.zh: 霸生咸，咸十九世孫澤，字季道，鴈門太守。

translations.literal: Ba bore Xian; in the nineteenth generation from Xian, his descendant Ze, styled Jidao, Governor of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Ba's son was Xian; in the nineteenth generation from Xian, his descendant Ze, styled Jidao, served as Governor of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 生昶，字文舒，魏司空、京陵穆侯。

translations.literal: He bore Chang, styled Wenshu, Minister of Works of Wei and Marquis Mu of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Chang, styled Wenshu, who served Wei as Minister of Works and held the title Marquis Mu of Jingling.

translations.literal: Two sons: Hun and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Hun and Ji.

sentences.zh: 渾字玄沖，晉錄尚書事、京陵元侯。

translations.literal: Hun, styled Xuanhong, recorded affairs of the Masters of Writing of Jin and Marquis Yuan of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Hun, styled Xuanhong, served Jin as Recorder of the Masters of Writing and held the title Marquis Yuan of Jingling.

translations.literal: He bore Zhan, styled Chuchong, Interior Administrator of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhan, styled Chuchong, who served as Interior Administrator of Runan.

sentences.zh: 生承，字安期，鎮東府從事中郎、藍田縣侯。

translations.literal: He bore Cheng, styled Anqi, Attendant Gentleman of the Eastern Pacification Headquarters and Marquis of Lantian County.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Cheng, styled Anqi, who served as Attendant Gentleman of the Eastern Pacification Headquarters and held the title Marquis of Lantian County.

sentences.zh: 生述，字懷祖，尚書令、藍田簡侯。

translations.literal: He bore Shu, styled Huaizu, Director of the Masters of Writing and Marquis Jian of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Shu, styled Huaizu, who served as Director of the Masters of Writing and held the title Marquis Jian of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 生坦之，字文度，左衞將軍、藍田獻侯。

translations.literal: He bore Tanzhi, styled Wendu, Left Guards General and Marquis Xian of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Tanzhi, styled Wendu, who served as Left Guards General and held the title Marquis Xian of Lantian.

translations.literal: He bore Yu, styled Maohe, Governor of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yu, styled Maohe, who served as Governor of Jiang Province.

translations.literal: He bore Ji, Attendant Cavalryman-at-Large.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Ji, who served as Attendant Cavalryman-at-Large.

sentences.zh: 生慧龍，後魏寧南將軍、長社穆侯。

translations.literal: He bore Huilong, General Who Pacifies the South of Later Wei and Marquis Mu of Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Huilong, who served Later Wei as General Who Pacifies the South and held the title Marquis Mu of Changshe.

translations.literal: He bore Baoxing, Dragon Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Baoxing, who served as Dragon Cavalry General.

translations.literal: He bore Qiong, styled Shizhen, General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Qiong, styled Shizhen, who served as General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 四子：遵業、廣業、延業、季和，號「四房王氏」。

translations.literal: Four sons: Zunye, Guangye, Yanye, and Jihe, called the "Four Branches of the Wang Clan."
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Zunye, Guangye, Yanye, and Jihe, known as the "Four Branches of the Wang Clan."

translations.literal: The Senior Branch of the Wang Clan
translations.idiomatic: The Senior Branch of the Wang Clan

translations.literal: The Second Branch of the Wang Clan
translations.idiomatic: The Second Branch of the Wang Clan

translations.literal: The Hedong Wang Clan:
translations.idiomatic: The Hedong Wang Clan:

sentences.zh: 烏丸王氏：霸長子殷，後漢中山太守，食邑祁縣。

translations.literal: The Wuhuan Wang Clan: Ba's eldest son Yin, Governor of Zhongshan of Later Han, with a fief at Qixian.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuhuan Wang Clan descended from Ba's eldest son Yin, who served Later Han as Governor of Zhongshan with a fief at Qixian.

translations.literal: In the fourth generation, his descendant Shi; three sons: Yun, Wei, and Mao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth generation, his descendant Shi had three sons: Yun, Wei, and Mao.

translations.literal: Mao, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Governor of You Province of Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: Mao served Later Han as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Governor of You Province.

sentences.zh: 六世孫光，後魏幷州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth generation, his descendant Guang, Governor of Bing Province of Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth generation, his descendant Guang served Later Wei as Governor of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 生冏，度支尚書、護烏丸校尉、廣陽侯，因號「烏丸王氏」。

translations.literal: He bore Jiong, Minister of Revenue, Protector of the Wuhuan, and Marquis of Guangyang; hence they were called the "Wuhuan Wang Clan."
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jiong, who served as Minister of Revenue and Protector of the Wuhuan and held the title Marquis of Guangyang; hence the line was called the "Wuhuan Wang Clan."

translations.literal: He bore Shennian.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Shennian.

translations.literal: When Northern Qi fell, the family moved to Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi fell, the family relocated to Wannian.

translations.literal: In the fifth generation from Jiong, his descendant Yuanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth generation from Jiong, his descendant was Yuanzheng.

translations.literal: The Zhongshan Wang clan also came from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhongshan Wang clan also traced its origin to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之亂，涼州參軍王軌子孫因居武威姑臧。

translations.literal: During the turmoil of the Yongjia era, the descendants of Wang Gui, Army Assistant of Liang Province, therefore settled at Gugang in Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: During the chaos of the Yongjia era, the descendants of Wang Gui, Army Assistant of Liang Province, settled at Gugang in Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 五世孫橋，字法生，侍御史、贈武威定王。

translations.literal: In the fifth generation, his descendant Qiao, styled Fasheng, Attendant Censor, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Ding of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth generation, his descendant Qiao, styled Fasheng, served as Attendant Censor and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Ding of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 生叡，封中山王，號「中山王氏」，後徙樂陵。

translations.literal: He bore Rui, enfeoffed as Prince of Zhongshan, called the "Zhongshan Wang Clan"; later [they] moved to Leling.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Rui, who was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhongshan; the line was known as the "Zhongshan Wang Clan," and later relocated to Leling.

sentences.zh: 汾州長史王滿，亦太原晉陽人，生大璡。

translations.literal: Wang Man, Chief Clerk of Fen Province, was also a native of Jinyang in Taiyuan; he bore Daqin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Man, Chief Clerk of Fen Province, was also from Jinyang in Taiyuan; his son was Daqin.

sentences.zh: 華陰王氏，後徙京兆新豐。

translations.literal: The Huayin Wang clan later moved to Xinfeng in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The Huayin Wang clan later relocated to Xinfeng in Jingzhao.

translations.literal: The Jingzhao Wang clan was traced to the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingzhao Wang clan descended from the Ji surname.

sentences.zh: 周文王少子畢公高之後，封魏，至昭王彤，生公子無忌，封信陵君。

translations.literal: Descendants of Duke Gao of Bi, the youngest son of King Wen of Zhou, were enfeoffed in Wei; down to King Zhao, Tong, who bore the prince-son Wuji, enfeoffed as Lord Xinling.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants of Duke Gao of Bi, the youngest son of King Wen of Zhou, were enfeoffed in Wei; reaching King Zhao, Tong, he bore Prince Wuji, who was enfeoffed as Lord Xinling.

translations.literal: Wuji bore Xianyou, who inherited the title of Lord Xinling.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji's son was Xianyou, who inherited the title of Lord Xinling.

sentences.zh: 秦滅魏，閒憂子卑子逃難于太山，漢高祖召為中涓，封蘭陵侯。

translations.literal: When Qin destroyed Wei, Xianyou's son Beizi fled to refuge at Mount Tai; Emperor Gaozu of Han summoned him as Attendant-at-the-Gate and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin destroyed Wei, Xianyou's son Beizi fled to Mount Tai for refuge; Emperor Gaozu of Han summoned him as Attendant-at-the-Gate and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 時人以其故王族也，謂之「王家」。

translations.literal: People of the time, because they were the former royal clan, called them the "Wang Family."
translations.idiomatic: People of the time, recognizing them as the former royal house, called them the "Wang Family."

sentences.zh: 卑子生悼，悼生賢，濟南太守，宣帝徙豪傑居霸陵，遂為京兆人。

translations.literal: Beizi bore Dao; Dao bore Xian, Governor of Jinan; Emperor Xuan relocated powerful families to Baling, and they thus became people of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Beizi's son was Dao, and Dao's son was Xian, who served as Governor of Jinan; when Emperor Xuan relocated powerful families to Baling, they thus became natives of Jingzhao.

translations.literal: In the seventh generation from Xian, his descendant Dang, Governor of Shang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh generation from Xian, his descendant Dang served as Governor of Shang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 卑子九世孫遵，字子春，後漢河南尹、上樂莊侯。

translations.literal: In the ninth generation from Beizi, his descendant Zun, styled Zichun, Intendant of Henan of Later Han and Marquis Zhuang of Shangle.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth generation from Beizi, his descendant Zun, styled Zichun, served Later Han as Intendant of Henan and held the title Marquis Zhuang of Shangle.

sentences.zh: 遵生魴，魴孫康，康生諶，諶生鵠。

translations.literal: Zun bore Fang; Fang's grandson was Kang; Kang bore Chen; Chen bore Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Zun's son was Fang; Fang's grandson was Kang; Kang's son was Chen; and Chen's son was Hu.

translations.literal: Fang's collateral descendant Jing bore Jun and Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: A collateral descendant of Fang, Jing, had two sons: Jun and Zhong.

sentences.zh: 均八世孫羆，至易從徙居汲郡。

translations.literal: In the eighth generation from Jun, his descendant Pi; down to Yicong, [the family] moved to Ji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth generation from Jun, his descendant Pi; by the time of Yicong, the family had relocated to Ji Commandery.

translations.literal: In the seventh generation from Zhong, his descendant Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh generation from Zhong, his descendant was Zhi.

sentences.zh: 王氏定著三房：　一曰琅邪王氏，二曰太原王氏，三曰京兆王氏。

translations.literal: The Wang clan was definitively established in three branches: the first called the Langya Wang clan, the second the Taiyuan Wang clan, and the third the Jingzhao Wang clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Wang clan was definitively divided into three branches: the Langya Wang clan, the Taiyuan Wang clan, and the Jingzhao Wang clan.

translations.literal: Thirteen chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: They produced thirteen chief ministers.

translations.literal: Of Langya there were Fangqing, Yu, Bo, and Xuan;
translations.idiomatic: From Langya came Fangqing, Yu, Bo, and Xuan;

sentences.zh: 太原有溥、縉、珪、涯、晙、播、鐸；

translations.literal: Of Taiyuan there were Pu, Jin, Gui, Ya, Jun, Bo, and Duo;
translations.idiomatic: From Taiyuan came Pu, Jin, Gui, Ya, Jun, Bo, and Duo;

translations.literal: Of Jingzhao there were Hui and Dezhen.
translations.idiomatic: From Jingzhao came Hui and Dezhen.

translations.literal: The Wei clan of the Wei surname was traced to the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei clan descended from the Ji surname.

sentences.zh: 周文王第十五子畢公高受封於畢，其後國絕，裔孫萬為晉獻公大夫，封於魏，河中河西縣是也，因為魏氏。

translations.literal: Duke Gao of Bi, the fifteenth son of King Wen of Zhou, received a fief at Bi; later the state was extinguished, and his descendant Wan served Duke Xian of Jin as Grandee and was enfeoffed at Wei—this is Hexi County in Hezhong—and thus they became the Wei clan.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Gao of Bi, the fifteenth son of King Wen of Zhou, received a fief at Bi; after the state was extinguished, his descendant Wan served Duke Xian of Jin as Grandee and was enfeoffed at Wei—present-day Hexi County in Hezhong—and the line became the Wei clan.

translations.idiomatic: Wan had two sons: Mang and Ji.

translations.idiomatic: His son was Jun.

translations.idiomatic: Jun's son was Hui.

translations.idiomatic: Hui had two sons: Bolun and Yan.

translations.literal: Yan, styled Shulun, Governor of Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, styled Shulun, served as Governor of Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 生歆，字子胡，鉅鹿太守，初居下曲陽。

translations.idiomatic: His son was Xin, styled Zihu, who served as Governor of Julu and first established himself at Xiaquyang.

translations.literal: The Guantao Wei clan was originally traced to Min, great-grandson of Heng, Inspector of Yan Province of Han; they first settled at Guantao.

translations.literal: The Wen clan of the Wen surname was traced to the Ji surname.
