sentences.zh: 唐叔虞之後，以公族封於河內溫，因以命氏。

translations.literal: Descendants of Prince Shu Yu of Tang, as a ducal house, were enfeoffed at Wen in Henei, and thus took that name as their clan.
translations.idiomatic: As descendants of Prince Shu Yu of Tang, they were enfeoffed at Wen in Henei as a ducal house and took Wen as their surname.

sentences.zh: 又郄至食采于溫，亦號溫季。

translations.literal: Also Xi Zhi's fief was at Wen, and he was also styled Wen Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zhi also held a fief at Wen and was likewise called Wen Ji.

sentences.zh: 漢有溫疥，封栒侯，謚曰順。

translations.literal: Under Han there was Wen Ke; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xun, with posthumous title Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han there was Wen Ke, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xun with the posthumous title Shun.

sentences.zh: 生仁，仁子何，始居太原祁縣。

translations.literal: He bore Ren; Ren's son was He, who first dwelt at Qi County in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Ren; Ren's son He first settled at Qi County in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 何六代孫序，字次房，後漢護羌校尉。

translations.literal: In the sixth generation from He, his descendant Xu, styled Cifang, Protector-General of the Qiang under Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth generation from He, his descendant Xu, styled Cifang, served Later Han as Protector-General of the Qiang.

translations.literal: Two sons: Shou and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Shou and Yi.

translations.literal: Shou, Chancellor of the Marquisate of Zouping.
translations.idiomatic: Shou served as Chancellor of the Marquisate of Zouping.

translations.literal: Yi, styled Boqi, Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, styled Boqi, served as Inspector of Yan Province.

translations.literal: He bore Shu; grandson Hui, Governor of Yang Province of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Shu; his grandson Hui served Wei as Governor of Yang Province.

translations.literal: He bore Gong, Governor of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Gong, who served as Governor of Jinan.

translations.literal: Gong had two sons: Xian and Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Gong had two sons: Xian and Dan.

translations.literal: Dan, Governor of Hedong under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Dan served Jin as Governor of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 生嶠，字太真，江州刺史、始安忠武公。

translations.literal: He bore Qiao, styled Taizhen, Inspector of Jiang Province and Duke Zhongwu of Shi'an.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Qiao, styled Taizhen, who served as Inspector of Jiang Province and Duke Zhongwu of Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 從子楷，隨桓謐奔于後魏。

translations.literal: Nephew Kai followed Huan Mi in fleeing to Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Kai followed Huan Mi in flight to Later Wei.

translations.literal: Eldest brother's grandson Qi, Governor of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother's grandson Qi served as Governor of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 曾孫裕，太中大夫，生君攸。

translations.literal: Great-grandson Yu, Grand Master for Consultation; he bore Junyou.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Yu, Grand Master for Consultation, had a son Junyou.

translations.literal: Of the Wen clan, one chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Wen clan produced one chief minister.

translations.literal: Yanbo.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo.

sentences.zh: 戴戴氏出自子姓，宋戴公之孫，以祖父謚為氏。

translations.literal: The Dai clan of the Dai surname was traced to the Zi surname; they were the grandson of Duke Dai of Song, who took their grandfather's posthumous title as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: The Dai clan descended from the Zi surname and traced its line to the grandson of Duke Dai of Song, who took his grandfather's posthumous title as the clan name.

sentences.zh: 至漢信都太傅戴德，世居魏郡斥丘。

translations.literal: When it came to Dai De, Grand Tutor of Xindu under Han, they had long resided at Chiqiu in Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of Dai De, Grand Tutor of Xindu under Han, the clan had long lived at Chiqiu in Wei Commandery.

translations.literal: Collateral descendant Jingzhen.
translations.idiomatic: His collateral descendant was Jingzhen.

translations.literal: Of the Dai clan, two chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Dai clan produced two chief ministers.

translations.literal: Zhou and Zhide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Zhide.

translations.literal: The Hou clan of the Hou surname was traced to the Si surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Hou clan descended from the Si surname.

sentences.zh: 夏后氏之裔封於侯，子孫因以為氏。

translations.literal: Descendants of the Xia house were enfeoffed at Hou, and their descendants thus took Hou as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants of the Xia house were enfeoffed at Hou, and their descendants took Hou as their surname.

sentences.zh: 一云本出姬姓，晉侯緡為曲沃武公所滅，子孫適於他國，以侯為氏。

translations.literal: One account says they were originally traced to the Ji surname; Marquis Min of Jin was destroyed by Duke Wu of Quwo, and his descendants went to other states, taking Hou as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: One tradition holds that they originally descended from the Ji surname: when Marquis Min of Jin was destroyed by Duke Wu of Quwo, his descendants fled to other states and took Hou as their surname.

translations.literal: In Zheng there was Hou Xuanduo; he bore Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In Zheng there was Hou Xuanduo, whose son was Jin.

sentences.zh: 漢末徙上谷，裔孫恕為北地太守，因家于北地三水。

translations.literal: At the end of Han they moved to Shanggu; collateral descendant Shu served as Governor of Beidi and made his home at Sanshui in Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Han the family moved to Shanggu; a collateral descendant, Shu, served as Governor of Beidi and established the family at Sanshui in Beidi.

sentences.zh: 四世孫植，從魏孝武西遷，賜姓侯伏氏，又賜姓賀吐氏，其後復舊。

translations.literal: In the fourth generation, his descendant Zhi followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei in the western migration; he was granted the surname Houfu, then granted the surname Hetu, and later the former name was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth generation, his descendant Zhi followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei in the western migration; he was granted the surnames Houfu and then Hetu in turn, but the original name was later restored.

translations.literal: Of the Hou clan, one chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Hou clan produced one chief minister.

translations.literal: Junji.
translations.idiomatic: Junji.

translations.literal: The Cen clan of the Cen surname was traced to the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Cen clan descended from the Ji surname.

sentences.zh: 周文王異母弟耀子渠，武王封為岑子，其地梁國北岑亭是也。

translations.literal: King Wen of Zhou's younger half-brother, Yao's son Qu, was enfeoffed by King Wu as Count of Cen—that place is Beicen Pavilion in the Liang state.
translations.idiomatic: Qu, son of Yao and younger half-brother of King Wen of Zhou, was enfeoffed by King Wu as Count of Cen—the site was Beicen Pavilion in the state of Liang.

sentences.zh: 子孫因以為氏，世居南陽棘陽。

translations.literal: His descendants thus took it as their clan name and long resided at Jiyang in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants took it as their surname and long lived at Jiyang in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 後漢有征南大將軍、舞陽壯侯岑彭，字君然。

translations.literal: Under Later Han there was General Who Conquers the South and Marquis Zhuang of Wuyang, Cen Peng, styled Junran.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Han there was Cen Peng, styled Junran, General Who Conquers the South and Marquis Zhuang of Wuyang.

translations.literal: He bore Zun, Commandant of Palace Cavalry and Marquis of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zun, Commandant of Palace Cavalry and Marquis of Xiyang.

translations.literal: Zun's great-grandson Xiang, Governor of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zun's great-grandson Xiang served as Governor of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 生晊，字公孝，黨錮難起，逃于江夏山中，徙居吳郡。

translations.literal: He bore Zhi, styled Gongxiao; when the Partisan Proscription troubles arose, he fled to the mountains of Jiangxia and moved to Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhi, styled Gongxiao; when the Partisan Proscription crisis erupted, he fled to the mountains of Jiangxia and later moved to Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 生亮伯，亮伯生軻，吳會稽鄱陽太守。

translations.literal: He bore Liangbo; Liangbo bore Ke, Governor of Poyang in Wu's Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Liangbo; Liangbo's son Ke served Wu as Governor of Poyang in Kuaiji.

translations.literal: Six sons: Chong, Hun, An, Song, Guang, and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: Chong, Hun, An, Song, Guang, and Yan.

translations.literal: Later they moved to Yanguan.
translations.idiomatic: Later they moved to Yanguan.

translations.literal: In the tenth generation, his descendant Shanfang.
translations.idiomatic: His tenth-generation descendant was Shanfang.

translations.literal: Of the Cen clan, three chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Cen clan produced three chief ministers.

translations.literal: Wenben, Xi, and Changqian.
translations.idiomatic: Wenben, Xi, and Changqian.

translations.literal: The Zhang clan of the Zhang surname was traced to the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang clan descended from the Ji surname.

sentences.zh: 黃帝子少昊青陽氏第五子揮為弓正，始制弓矢，子孫賜姓張氏。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor's son Shaohao of the Qingyang clan—his fifth son Hui served as Master of the Bow, first fashioned bow and arrow, and his descendants were granted the surname Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Shaohao of the Qingyang clan, son of the Yellow Emperor, had a fifth son Hui who served as Master of the Bow, first devised bow and arrow, and whose descendants were granted the surname Zhang.

sentences.zh: 周宣王時有卿士張仲，其後裔事晉為大夫。

translations.literal: In the time of King Xuan of Zhou there was Minister Zhang Zhong; his descendants served Jin as Grandees.
translations.idiomatic: In the time of King Xuan of Zhou there was Minister Zhang Zhong, whose descendants served Jin as grandees.

sentences.zh: 張侯生老，老生趯，趯生骼。

translations.literal: Marquis Zhang bore Lao; Lao bore Yue; Yue bore Ge.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Zhang's son was Lao; Lao's son was Yue; Yue's son was Ge.

translations.literal: When the Three Clans divided Jin, the Zhang clan served Han.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Clans divided Jin, the Zhang clan entered the service of Han.

sentences.zh: 韓相張開地，生平，凡相五君。

translations.literal: Han Chancellor Zhang Kaidi bore Ping, who in all served five rulers as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Han Chancellor Zhang Kaidi had a son Ping, who in all served five rulers as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 平生良，字子房，漢留文成侯。

translations.literal: Ping's son was Liang, styled Zifang, Marquis of Liuwen under Han.
translations.idiomatic: Ping's son was Liang, styled Zifang, Marquis of Liuwen under Han.

translations.literal: Liang bore Buyi.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's son was Buyi.

translations.literal: Buyi bore Dian.
translations.idiomatic: Buyi's son was Dian.

translations.literal: Dian bore Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Dian's son was Mo.

translations.literal: Mo bore Jin, Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Mo's son was Jin, Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 金生陽陵公乘千秋，字萬雅。

translations.literal: Jin bore Lord Qianqiu of Yangling, styled Wanya.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's son was Lord Qianqiu of Yangling, styled Wanya.

translations.literal: Qianqiu bore Song.
translations.idiomatic: Qianqiu's son was Song.

translations.literal: Song had five sons: Zhuang, Zan, Peng, Mu, and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Song had five sons: Zhuang, Zan, Peng, Mu, and Shu.

translations.literal: Zhuang bore Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang's son was Yin.

sentences.zh: 胤生皓，字叔明，後漢司空，世居武陽犍為。

translations.literal: Yin bore Hao, styled Shuming, Minister of Works under Later Han; the clan long resided at Jianwei in Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's son was Hao, styled Shuming, who served Later Han as Minister of Works; the clan long lived at Jianwei in Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 皓生宇，北平、范陽太守，避地居方城。

translations.literal: Hao bore Yu, Governor of Beiping and Fanyang; he took refuge and dwelt at Fangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's son was Yu, who served as Governor of Beiping and Fanyang; he took refuge and settled at Fangcheng.

translations.literal: Yu's grandson, Marquis of Feiru, Mengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's grandson was Mengcheng, Marquis of Feiru.

translations.literal: Mengcheng's son was Ping, Administrator of Yuyang Commandery under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Mengcheng's son Ping served Wei as Administrator of Yuyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 平生華，字茂先，晉司空、壯武公。

translations.literal: Ping's son was Hua, styled Maoxian, Minister of Works and Duke Zhuangwu of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Ping's son was Hua, styled Maoxian, who served Jin as Minister of Works and Duke Zhuangwu.

translations.literal: Two sons: Yi and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Yi and Wei.

translations.literal: Yi, styled Yanzhong, Attendant Gentleman of the Palace Horse.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, styled Yanzhong, served as Attendant Gentleman of the Palace Horse.

sentences.zh: 生輿，字公安，太子舍人，襲壯武公。

translations.literal: He bore Yu, styled Gong'an, Aide to the Heir Apparent; he inherited the title Duke Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yu, styled Gong'an, who served as Aide to the Heir Apparent and inherited the title Duke Zhuangwu.

translations.literal: He bore Cihui, Governor of Puyang under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Cihui, who served Song as Governor of Puyang.

translations.literal: Two sons: Muzhi and Anzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Muzhi and Anzhi.

translations.literal: Anzhi's branch moved and dwelt at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhi's branch moved to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 韙，晉散騎常侍，隨元帝南遷，寓居江左。

translations.literal: Wei served Jin as Regular Palace Attendant; he followed Emperor Yuan in the southward migration and sojourned on the left bank of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei served Jin as Regular Palace Attendant; he followed Emperor Yuan in the southward migration and settled on the left bank of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 六世孫隆，太常卿，復還河東，後徙洛陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth generation, his descendant Long, Minister of Ceremonies, returned to Hedong and later moved to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth generation, his descendant Long, Minister of Ceremonies, returned to Hedong and later moved to Luoyang.

translations.literal: He bore Zifan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zifan.

translations.literal: Zifan bore Jun, Attendant of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Zifan's son Jun served as Attendant of Hedong.

translations.literal: He bore Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yi.

sentences.zh: 河東張氏本出晉司空華裔孫吒子，隋河東郡丞，自范陽徙居河東猗氏，生長度。

translations.literal: The Hedong Zhang clan was originally traced to Tuozi, collateral descendant of Minister of Works Hua of Jin, Assistant Administrator of Hedong Commandery under Sui; he moved from Fanyang and dwelt at Yishi in Hedong, and bore Changdu.
translations.idiomatic: The Hedong Zhang clan originally descended from Tuozi, a collateral descendant of Jin Minister of Works Hua, who served Sui as Assistant Administrator of Hedong Commandery, moved from Fanyang to Yishi in Hedong, and had a son Changdu.

sentences.zh: 始興張氏亦出自晉司空華之後，隨晉南遷，至君政，因官居于韶州曲江。

translations.literal: The Shixing Zhang clan also came from descendants of Minister of Works Hua of Jin; they followed Jin in the southward migration, and when it came to Junzheng, because of office they dwelt at Qujiang in Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Shixing Zhang clan also descended from Jin Minister of Works Hua; they followed the Jin court south, and by the time of Junzheng had settled at Qujiang in Shaozhou through official appointment.

sentences.zh: 馮翊張氏本出後漢司空皓少子綱，字文紀，後漢廣陵太守。

translations.literal: The Fengyi Zhang clan was originally traced to Gang, youngest son of Minister of Works Hao of Later Han, styled Wenji, Governor of Guangling under Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: The Fengyi Zhang clan originally descended from Gang, youngest son of Later Han Minister of Works Hao, styled Wenji, who served Later Han as Governor of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 曾孫翼，字伯恭，蜀冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Great-grandson Yi, styled Bogong, Inspector of Ji Province of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Yi, styled Bogong, served Shu as Inspector of Ji Province.

translations.literal: Descendants moved from Jianwei to Xiagui.
translations.idiomatic: The descendants moved from Jianwei to Xiagui.

sentences.zh: 吳郡張氏本出嵩第四子睦，字選公，後漢蜀郡太守，始居吳郡。

translations.literal: The Wu Commandery Zhang clan was originally traced to Mu, fourth son of Song, styled Xuangong, Governor of Shu Commandery under Later Han; they first settled in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Commandery Zhang clan originally descended from Mu, Song's fourth son, styled Xuangong, who served Later Han as Governor of Shu Commandery and first established the family in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 裔孫顯，齊廬江太守，生紹。

translations.literal: Collateral descendant Xian, Governor of Lujiang under Qi; he bore Shao.
translations.idiomatic: A collateral descendant, Xian, served Qi as Governor of Lujiang and had a son Shao.

sentences.zh: 清河東武城張氏本出漢留侯良裔孫司徒歆。

translations.literal: The Qinghe Dongwucheng Zhang clan was originally traced to Xin, Chancellor of State, collateral descendant of Marquis of Liu, Liang, under Han.
translations.idiomatic: The Qinghe Dongwucheng Zhang clan originally descended from Xin, Chancellor of State and collateral descendant of Han Marquis of Liu, Liang.

translations.literal: Xin's younger brother was Xie, styled Jiqing, Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's younger brother Xie, styled Jiqing, served as Commandant of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 生魏太山太守岱，自河內徙清河。

translations.literal: He bore Dai, Governor of Taishan under Wei; he moved from Henei to Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Dai, who served Wei as Governor of Taishan and moved the family from Henei to Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 曾孫幸，後魏青州刺史、平陸侯。

translations.literal: Great-grandson Xing, Governor of Qing Province and Marquis of Pinglu under Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Xing served Later Wei as Governor of Qing Province and Marquis of Pinglu.

translations.literal: He bore Zhun, Eastern Inspector of Qing Province; he inherited the marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhun, Eastern Inspector of Qing Province, who inherited the marquisate.

translations.literal: He bore Lingzhen.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Lingzhen.

translations.literal: He bore Yi; at the end of Sui, [the family] moved to Changle in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yi; at the end of the Sui dynasty, the family moved to Changle in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 河間張氏，漢常山景王耳之後，世居鄚縣。

translations.literal: The Hejian Zhang clan were descendants of Ear, Prince Jing of Changshan under Han, and for generations dwelt at Mo County.
translations.idiomatic: The Hejian Zhang clan descended from Ear, Prince Jing of Changshan under Han, and had lived for generations at Mo County.

sentences.zh: 後周有司成中大夫、虞鄉定公張羨，賜姓叱羅氏。

translations.literal: Later Zhou had Zhang Xian, Master of the Masters of the Masters, Palace Officer, Duke Ding of Yuxiang, who was granted the surname Chiluo.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Zhou there was Zhang Xian, Master of the Masters of the Masters, Palace Officer, and Duke Ding of Yuxiang, who was granted the surname Chiluo.

sentences.zh: 生照，照字士鴻，隋冀州刺史，復為張氏。

translations.literal: He bore Zhao; Zhao was styled Shihong, Governor of Jizhou under Sui, and again became Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhao, styled Shihong, who served Sui as Governor of Jizhou and restored the surname Zhang.

translations.literal: Three sons: Huibao, Huiyao, and Huizhen.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Huibao, Huiyao, and Huizhen.

sentences.zh: 中山張氏出漢北平文侯倉之後，世居中山義豐。

translations.literal: The Zhongshan Zhang clan came from descendants of Cang, Marquis Wen of Beiping under Han, and for generations dwelt at Yifeng in Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhongshan Zhang clan descended from Cang, Marquis Wen of Beiping under Han, and had lived for generations at Yifeng in Zhongshan.

translations.literal: The Wei Commandery Zhang clan for generations dwelt at Fanshui.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Commandery Zhang clan had lived for generations at Fanshui.

translations.literal: The Ji Commandery Zhang clan for generations dwelt at Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Ji Commandery Zhang clan had lived for generations at Pingyuan.

translations.literal: The Zhengzhou Zhang Clan:
translations.idiomatic: The Zhengzhou Zhang Clan:

translations.literal: Of the Zhang clan, seventeen chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang clan produced seventeen chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 柬之、說、嘉貞、延賞、弘靖、九齡、仁愿、鎰、錫、文瓘、光輔、文蔚、濬、行成、大安、鎬、亮。

translations.literal: Jianzhi, Yue, Jiazhen, Yanshang, Hongjing, Jiuling, Renyuan, Yi, Xi, Wenguan, Guangfu, Wenwei, Jun, Xingcheng, Da'an, Hao, and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: They were Jianzhi, Yue, Jiazhen, Yanshang, Hongjing, Jiuling, Renyuan, Yi, Xi, Wenguan, Guangfu, Wenwei, Jun, Xingcheng, Da'an, Hao, and Liang.

sentences.zh: 馬馬氏出自嬴姓，伯益之後。

translations.literal: The Ma clan of the Ma surname was traced to the Ying surname; they were descendants of Boyi.
translations.idiomatic: The Ma clan descended from the Ying surname and traced its line to Boyi.

sentences.zh: 趙王子趙奢為惠文王將，封馬服君，生牧，亦為趙將，子孫因以為氏，世居邯鄲。

translations.literal: Zhao's son Prince Zhao She served as a general for King Huiwen, was enfeoffed as Lord of Mafu, and bore Mu, who also served as a general of Zhao; their descendants therefore took this as their clan name and for generations dwelt at Handan.
translations.idiomatic: A son of the Zhao royal house, Zhao She, served King Huiwen of Zhao as a general and was enfeoffed as Lord of Mafu. His son Mu also served Zhao as a general, and the family took Ma as its surname and lived for generations at Handan.

sentences.zh: 秦滅趙，牧子興徙咸陽，秦封武安侯。

translations.literal: When Qin destroyed Zhao, Mu's son Xing moved to Xianyang, and Qin enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin conquered Zhao, Mu's son Xing moved to Xianyang, where Qin enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wu'an.

translations.literal: Three sons: Gui, Chen, and Song.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Gui, Chen, and Song.

sentences.zh: 嵩生述，字貞惠，漢太子大夫、平通侯。

translations.literal: Song bore Shu, styled Zhenhui, Grand Master for the Heir Apparent of Han and Marquis of Pingtong.
translations.idiomatic: Song's son Shu, styled Zhenhui, served Han as Grand Master for the Heir Apparent and held the title Marquis of Pingtong.

translations.literal: He bore Quan, who served as General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: His son Quan served as General Who Pacifies the East.

translations.literal: Three sons: Heluo, Tong, and Lun.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Heluo, Tong, and Lun.

sentences.zh: 通字達，黃門郎、侍中、重合侯，坐何羅反，徙扶風茂陵成懽里。

translations.literal: Tong was styled Da, Palace Attendant, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Marquis of Chonghe; implicated in Heluo's rebellion, he was moved to Chenghuan Lane at Maoling in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Tong, styled Da, served as Palace Attendant and Attendant-in-Ordinary and was Marquis of Chonghe. Because of Heluo's rebellion, he was relocated to Chenghuan Lane at Maoling in Fufeng.

translations.literal: He bore Bin, Consultant and Imperial Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bin served as Consultant and Imperial Inspector.

translations.literal: Three sons: Qing, Chang, and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Qing, Chang, and Xiang.

translations.literal: Chang bore Zhong, Marshal of the Northern Army.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's son Zhong served as Marshal of the Northern Army.

translations.literal: Four sons: Kuang, Yu, Yuan, and Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Kuang, Yu, Yuan, and Yuan.

sentences.zh: 余字聖卿，中壘校尉、揚州牧。

translations.literal: Yu was styled Shengqing, Colonel of the Central Rampart and Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, styled Shengqing, served as Colonel of the Central Rampart and Governor of Yangzhou.

translations.literal: Two sons: Yan and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Yan and Fu.

sentences.zh: 嚴字威卿，後漢將作大匠。

translations.literal: Yan was styled Weiqing, Master of Works under Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, styled Weiqing, served Later Han as Master of Works.

translations.literal: Seven sons: Gu, Kang, Xin, Zhuan, Rong, Liu, and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons: Gu, Kang, Xin, Zhuan, Rong, Liu, and Xu.

sentences.zh: 歆十一世孫默，十二世孫岫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh generation from Xin was Mo; in the twelfth generation was Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh generation from Xin came Mo; in the twelfth came Xiu.

translations.literal: The Fufeng Ma Clan:
translations.idiomatic: The Fufeng Ma Clan:

sentences.zh: 茌平馬氏，北齊有茌平令暹，因家焉。

translations.literal: The Chiping Ma clan: under Northern Qi there was Xian, Magistrate of Chiping, who made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: The Chiping Ma clan: under Northern Qi, Xian served as Magistrate of Chiping and established his household there.

translations.literal: Of the Ma clan, three chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Ma clan produced three chief ministers.

translations.literal: Sui, Zhi, and Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: They were Sui, Zhi, and Zhou.

translations.literal: The Chu clan of the Chu surname was traced to the Zi surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Chu clan descended from the Zi surname.

sentences.zh: 宋共公子段，字子石，食采於褚，其德可師，號曰「褚師」，生公孫肥，子孫因為褚氏。

translations.literal: Prince Duan, son of Duke Gong of Song, styled Zishi, received his fief at Chu; his virtue was worthy of emulation, and he was called "Master Chu"; he bore Gongsun Fei, and his descendants therefore became the Chu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Duan of Song, styled Zishi, held his fief at Chu, and because his conduct was worthy of emulation he was known as Master Chu. His son Gongsun Fei founded the line, and the family took Chu as its surname.

sentences.zh: 漢梁相褚大，元、成間有褚先生少孫，裔孫重，始居河南陽翟。

translations.literal: Under Han, Chu Da served as Chancellor of Liang; during the Yuans and Cheng reigns there was Master Chu Shaosun; collateral descendant Chong first dwelt at Yangzhai in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han, Chu Da served as Chancellor of Liang; during the Yuans and Cheng reigns there was Master Chu Shaosun; and collateral descendant Chong first established the family at Yangzhai in Henan.

sentences.zh: 裔孫招，安東將軍、揚州都督、關內侯。

translations.literal: Collateral descendant Zhao served as General Who Pacifies the East, Area Commander of Yangzhou, and Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Collateral descendant Zhao served as General Who Pacifies the East, Area Commander of Yangzhou, and held the title Marquis Within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 孫䂮，字武良，晉安東將軍，始徙丹楊。

translations.literal: His grandson Ji, styled Wuliang, served Jin as General Who Pacifies the East and first moved to Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Ji, styled Wuliang, served Jin as General Who Pacifies the East and first relocated the family to Danyang.

translations.literal: Five sons: Wei, Yue, Qia, Yu, and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Wei, Yue, Qia, Yu, and Xiang.

translations.literal: Qia served as Governor of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Qia served as Governor of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 生征討大都督、都鄉元穆侯裒，字季野。

translations.literal: He bore Bao, styled Jiye, Grand Chief of Campaigns and Pacification and Marquis Yuanmu of Duxiang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bao, styled Jiye, served as Grand Chief of Campaigns and Pacification and held the title Marquis Yuanmu of Duxiang.

translations.literal: Two sons: Xin and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Xin and Xi.

translations.literal: Xin was styled You'an, Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xin, styled You'an, served as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 生爽，字義弘，會稽王諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He bore Shuang, styled Yihong, Adviser to the King of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shuang, styled Yihong, served as Adviser to the King of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 爽五子：秀之、粹之、陟之、裕之、淡之。

translations.literal: Shuang had five sons: Xiuzhi, Cuizhi, Zhizhi, Yuzhi, and Danzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang had five sons: Xiuzhi, Cuizhi, Zhizhi, Yuzhi, and Danzhi.

translations.literal: Xiuzhi was styled Changqian, Minister of Ceremonies under Song.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi, styled Changqian, served Song as Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 四子：儶之、湛之、貞之、法顯。

translations.literal: Four sons: Huizhi, Zhanshi, Zhenzhi, and Faxian.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Huizhi, Zhanshi, Zhenzhi, and Faxian.

translations.literal: Of the Chu clan, one chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Chu clan produced one chief minister.

translations.literal: Suiliang.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang.

translations.literal: The Cui clan of the Cui surname was traced to the Jiang surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Cui clan descended from the Jiang surname.

sentences.zh: 齊丁公伋嫡子季子讓國叔乙，食采於崔，遂為崔氏。

translations.literal: Duke Ding Ji of Qi had a legitimate younger son who yielded the state to Uncle Yi; receiving his fief at Cui, he thus became the Cui clan.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Ding Ji of Qi had a legitimate younger son who yielded the realm to Uncle Yi; having received his fief at Cui, Uncle Yi became the founder of the Cui clan.

sentences.zh: 濟南東朝陽縣西北有崔氏城是也。

translations.literal: Northwest of Dongyang County in Jinan there is the City of the Cui clan—this is the place.
translations.idiomatic: The City of the Cui clan lay northwest of Dongyang County in Jinan.

translations.literal: The younger son bore Duke Mu.
translations.idiomatic: The younger son had a son, Duke Mu.

translations.literal: Duke Mu bore Wo.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Mu's son was Wo.

translations.literal: Wo bore Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Wo's son was Ye.

sentences.zh: 八世孫夭生杼，為齊正卿。

translations.literal: In the eighth generation, his descendant Yao bore Zhu, who served as Chief Minister of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth generation, his descendant Yao had a son Zhu, who served Qi as Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 生子成、子明、子彊，皆為慶封所殺。

translations.literal: He bore Zicheng, Ziming, and Ziqiang; all were killed by Qing Feng.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons—Zicheng, Ziming, and Ziqiang—all of whom were killed by Qing Feng.

translations.literal: Ziming fled to Lu and bore Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Ziming fled to Lu, and his son was Liang.

sentences.zh: 十五世孫意如，為秦大夫，封東萊侯。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth generation, his descendant Yiru served as a grandee of Qin and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth generation, his descendant Yiru served Qin as a grandee and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Donglai.

translations.literal: Two sons: Ye and Zhongmou.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Ye and Zhongmou.

sentences.zh: 業字伯基，漢東萊侯，居清河東武城。

translations.literal: Ye was styled Boji, Marquis of Donglai under Han, and dwelt at Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Ye, styled Boji, held the title Marquis of Donglai under Han and settled at Dongwucheng in Qinghe.

translations.literal: He bore Yu, Marquis Xin of the Ministry of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu held the title Marquis Xin of the Ministry of Ceremonies.

translations.literal: Yu bore Shao, Marquis Mu, Governor of Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's son Shao served as Governor of Xiangguo and held the title Marquis Mu.

translations.literal: Shao bore Ya, Household Minister and Marquis Si.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's son Ya served as Household Minister and held the title Marquis Si.

translations.literal: Ya bore Zhong, Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ya's son Zhong served as Governor of Yangzhou.

translations.literal: Zhong bore Tai, Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's son Tai served as Regular Palace Attendant.

translations.literal: Tai was styled Shirong and first dwelt at Yu County.
translations.idiomatic: Tai, styled Shirong, first established the family at Yu County.

translations.literal: Two sons: Ke and Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Ke and Jing.

sentences.zh: 恪，丞相司直，生郡功曹殷。

translations.literal: Ke served as Rectifier under the Chancellor and bore Yin, Merit Officer of the Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ke served as Rectifier under the Chancellor, and his son Yin served as Merit Officer of the Commandery.

translations.literal: Seven sons: Shuang, Han, Yu, Jin, Hu, Fan, and Gu.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons: Shuang, Han, Yu, Jin, Hu, Fan, and Gu.

sentences.zh: 雙為東祖，邯為西祖，㝢為南祖，亦號中祖。

translations.literal: Shuang was made the Eastern Branch, Han was made the Western Branch, Yu was made the Southern Branch, and was also styled the Central Branch.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang was designated the Eastern Branch, Han the Western Branch, and Yu the Southern Branch, also known as the Central Branch.

sentences.zh: 㝢四世孫林，字德儒，魏司空、安陽孝侯。

translations.literal: In the fourth generation from Yu was Lin, styled Deru, Minister of Works of Wei and Marquis Xiao of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth generation from Yu came Lin, styled Deru, who served Wei as Minister of Works and held the title Marquis Xiao of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 曾孫悅，前趙司徒、左長史、關內侯。

translations.literal: His great-grandson Yue served Former Zhao as Minister over the Masses, Left Chief Clerk, and Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Yue served Former Zhao as Minister over the Masses and Left Chief Clerk and held the title Marquis Within the Passes.

translations.literal: Three sons: Hun, Qian, and Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Hun, Qian, and Zhan.

sentences.zh: 湛生顗，後魏平東府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Zhan bore Yan, Adviser to the Eastern Pacification Headquarters under Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's son Yan served Later Wei as Adviser to the Eastern Pacification Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 生蔚，自宋奔後魏，居滎陽，號鄭州崔氏。

translations.literal: He bore Wei; fleeing from Song to Later Wei, they dwelt at Xingyang and were styled the Zhengzhou Cui clan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wei fled from Song to Later Wei, settled at Xingyang, and founded the Zhengzhou Cui clan.

sentences.zh: 許州鄢陵房：蔚少子彧，居鄢陵。

translations.literal: The Xuzhou Yanling branch: Wei's youngest son Yu dwelt at Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuzhou Yanling branch: Wei's youngest son Yu settled at Yanling.

sentences.zh: 南祖崔氏：泰少子景，字子成，淮陽太守，生挺，字子建。

translations.literal: The Southern Branch Cui clan: Tai's youngest son Jing, styled Zicheng, Governor of Huaiyang, bore Ting, styled Zijian.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Branch Cui clan: Tai's youngest son Jing, styled Zicheng, served as Governor of Huaiyang, and his son was Ting, styled Zijian.

translations.literal: Ting bore Quan, General Who Breaks Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Ting's son Quan served as General Who Breaks Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 權生諫議大夫濟，字元先，亦稱南祖。

translations.literal: Quan bore Ji, styled Yuanxian, Grand Master of Remonstrance, who was also called the Southern Branch.
translations.idiomatic: Quan's son Ji, styled Yuanxian, served as Grand Master of Remonstrance and was also known as the Southern Branch.

translations.literal: Ji bore Qiu, styled Daochu.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's son was Qiu, styled Daochu.

translations.literal: Qiu bore Rong, styled Zichang, Marquis of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu's son Rong, styled Zichang, held the title Marquis of Anding.

translations.literal: Rong bore Wen, styled Daohe, Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's son Wen, styled Daohe, served as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 溫生魏常山太守就，字伯玄。

translations.literal: Wen bore Jiu, styled Boxuan, Governor of Changshan under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wen's son Jiu, styled Boxuan, served Wei as Governor of Changshan.

translations.literal: Jiu bore Gong'an, Governor of Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiu's son Gong'an served as Governor of Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 公安生晉大司徒、關內侯岳，字元嵩。

translations.literal: Gong'an bore Yue, styled Yuansong, Minister over the Masses of Jin and Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Gong'an's son Yue, styled Yuansong, served Jin as Minister over the Masses and held the title Marquis Within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 岳生後趙尚書右僕射牧，字伯蘭。

translations.literal: Yue bore Mu, styled Bolan, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing under Later Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's son Mu, styled Bolan, served Later Zhao as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 牧生後趙征東大將軍蔭，字道崇。

translations.literal: Mu bore Yin, styled Daochong, Grand General Who Campaigns East under Later Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Mu's son Yin, styled Daochong, served Later Zhao as Grand General Who Campaigns East.

translations.literal: Yin bore Yi, styled Shaoye, Magistrate of Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's son Yi, styled Shaoye, served as Magistrate of Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 怡生宋樂陵太守曠，隨慕容德度河居齊郡烏水，號烏水房。

translations.literal: Yi bore Kuang, Governor of Leling under Song; following Murong De across the river, he dwelt at Wushui in Qi Commandery and was styled the Wushui branch.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's son Kuang served Song as Governor of Leling; following Murong De across the river, he settled at Wushui in Qi Commandery and founded the Wushui branch.

sentences.zh: 生清河太守二子：靈延、靈茂。

translations.literal: He bore the Governor of Qinghe, who had two sons: Lingyan and Lingmao.
translations.idiomatic: His son served as Governor of Qinghe and had two sons: Lingyan and Lingmao.

sentences.zh: 靈茂，宋庫部郎中，居全節。

translations.literal: Lingmao served Song as Director in the Ministry of Storehouses and dwelt at Quanjie.
translations.idiomatic: Lingmao served Song as Director in the Ministry of Storehouses and settled at Quanjie.

sentences.zh: 生稚寶，稚寶，後魏祠部郎中。

translations.literal: He bore Zhibao; Zhibao served Later Wei as Director in the Sacrificial Regimen.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhibao, who served Later Wei as Director in the Sacrificial Regimen.

sentences.zh: 生逵，字景通，北齊三公郎中。

translations.literal: He bore Kui, styled Jingtong, Director in the Three Dukes under Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kui, styled Jingtong, served Northern Qi as Director in the Three Dukes.

translations.literal: He bore Deren, Chief Clerk to the Minister over the Masses of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Deren served as Chief Clerk to the Minister over the Masses of Northern Zhou.

translations.literal: Deren bore Junshi.
translations.idiomatic: Deren's son was Junshi.

translations.literal: In the eighth generation from Boji was Mi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth generation from Boji came Mi.

translations.literal: Mi had two sons: Ba and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Mi had two sons: Ba and Yan.

translations.literal: Ba's great-grandson was Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Ba's great-grandson was Zun.

translations.literal: Yan was styled Jigui, Director of the Masters of Writing under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, styled Jigui, served Wei as Director of the Masters of Writing.

translations.literal: He bore Liang, styled Shiwen.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Liang, styled Shiwen.

translations.literal: He bore Yu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yu.

translations.literal: Yu bore Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's son was Yu.

translations.literal: Yu bore Cheng, styled Shuzu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's son Cheng was styled Shuzu.

translations.literal: Cheng bore Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's son was Yi.

translations.literal: In the fourth generation from Yi was Gai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth generation from Yi came Gai.

sentences.zh: 清河大房：逞少子諲，宋青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: The Qinghe Major Branch: Cheng's youngest son Shen, Governors of Qing and Ji provinces under Song.
translations.idiomatic: The Qinghe Major Branch: Cheng's youngest son Shen served Song as Governor of Qing and Ji provinces.

sentences.zh: 生靈和，宋員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He bore Linghe, Supernumerary Regular Attendant of Fast Cavalry under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His son Linghe served Song as Supernumerary Regular Attendant of Fast Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 生後魏贈清河太守宗伯。

translations.literal: He bore Zongbo, posthumously enfeoffed as Governor of Qinghe under Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongbo was posthumously granted the title Governor of Qinghe under Later Wei.

translations.literal: He bore Xiu and Yin.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Xiu and Yin.

translations.literal: Xiu was styled the Major Branch.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu founded the Major Branch.

sentences.zh: 清河小房：寅字敬禮，後魏太子舍人、樂安郡守。

translations.literal: The Qinghe Minor Branch: Yin was styled Jingli, Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Administrator of Lean Commandery under Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Qinghe Minor Branch: Yin, styled Jingli, served Later Wei as Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Administrator of Lean Commandery.

sentences.zh: 生長謙，給事中、青州刺史，生子令、公華。

translations.literal: He bore Zhangqian, Attendant at the Gate and Governor of Qing Province; he bore Ziling and Gonghua.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhangqian served as Attendant at the Gate and Governor of Qing Province and had two sons: Ziling and Gonghua.

translations.literal: The Qinghe Qingzhou Branch: Yan bore Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The Qinghe Qingzhou Branch: Yan's son was Qin.

translations.literal: Qin bore Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's son was Jing.

translations.literal: Jing's grandson was Qiong, aide to the Cavalry General under Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's grandson Qiong served Murong Chui as aide to the Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 生輯，宋泰山太守，徙居青州，號青州房。

translations.literal: He bore Ji, Governor of Taishan under Song; moving to Qingzhou, he was styled the Qingzhou Branch.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji served Song as Governor of Taishan, moved to Qingzhou, and founded the Qingzhou Branch.

translations.literal: Ji bore Xiuzhi and Mulian.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had two sons: Xiuzhi and Mulian.

sentences.zh: 博陵安平崔氏：仲牟生融。

translations.literal: The Boling Anping Cui clan: Zhongmou bore Rong.
translations.idiomatic: The Boling Anping Cui clan: Zhongmou's son was Rong.

translations.literal: Rong bore Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's son was Shi.

translations.literal: Shi bore Kuo, styled Shaotong; Kuo bore Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's son Kuo, styled Shaotong, had a son named Ji.

translations.literal: Ji bore Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's son was Qin.

translations.literal: Qin bore Chao, Attendant Censor of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's son Chao served Han as Attendant Censor.

translations.literal: He bore Shu, Governor of four commanderies under Han.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shu served Han as Governor of four commanderies.

translations.literal: Two sons: Fa and Zhuan.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Fa and Zhuan.

translations.literal: Zhuan served as Commandery Scholar and bore Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuan served as Commandery Scholar, and his son was Yi.

translations.literal: Yi bore Yin, styled Tingbo, Prefect of Changcen.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's son Yin, styled Tingbo, served as Prefect of Changcen.

translations.literal: Two sons: Pan and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Pan and Shi.

sentences.zh: 盤生烈，後漢太尉、城門校尉。

translations.literal: Pan bore Lie, Grand Commandant and Colonel of the City Gates under Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: Pan's son Lie served Later Han as Grand Commandant and Colonel of the City Gates.

translations.literal: He bore Jun, styled Zhouping, Governor of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jun, styled Zhouping, served as Governor of Xihe.

translations.literal: In the tenth generation, his descendant Ang.
translations.idiomatic: His tenth-generation descendant was Ang.

sentences.zh: 大房崔氏：駰少子寔，字子真，後漢尚書，生皓。

translations.literal: The Major Branch Cui clan: Yin's youngest son Shi, styled Zizhen, Director of the Masters of Writing under Later Han, bore Hao.
translations.idiomatic: The Major Branch Cui clan: Yin's youngest son Shi, styled Zizhen, served Later Han as Director of the Masters of Writing, and his son was Hao.

translations.literal: Hao bore Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's son was Zhi.

translations.literal: Zhi bore Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's son was Zan.

sentences.zh: 讚生洪，字良夫，晉大司農。

translations.literal: Zan bore Hong, styled Liangfu, Grand Minister of Agriculture of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Zan's son Hong, styled Liangfu, served Jin as Grand Minister of Agriculture.

translations.literal: He bore Kuo.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Kuo.

translations.literal: Kuo bore Chuan.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo's son was Chuan.

translations.literal: Chuan bore Yi, styled Shimao.
translations.idiomatic: Chuan's son Yi was styled Shimao.

sentences.zh: 五子：連、琨、格、邈、殊，又三子：怡、豹、偘為一房，號「六房」。

translations.literal: Five sons: Lian, Kun, Ge, Miao, and Shu; three further sons—Yi, Bao, and Kan—formed one branch, styled the "Six Branches."
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Lian, Kun, Ge, Miao, and Shu; three further sons—Yi, Bao, and Kan—together formed one branch known as the "Six Branches."

sentences.zh: 連字景遇，鉅鹿令，號「大房」。

translations.literal: Lian was styled Jingyu, Magistrate of Julu, and was styled the "Major Branch."
translations.idiomatic: Lian, styled Jingyu, served as Magistrate of Julu and founded the "Major Branch."

translations.literal: He bore Chuo, Merit Officer of the Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chuo served as Merit Officer of the Commandery.

translations.literal: Two sons: Biao and Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Biao and Jian.

translations.literal: Biao was styled Luozu, acting Governor of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Biao, styled Luozu, served as acting Governor of Boling.

sentences.zh: 生後魏鎮南長史廣，字仲慶。

translations.literal: He bore Guang, styled Zhongqing, Southern Garrison Chief Clerk under Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guang, styled Zhongqing, served Later Wei as Southern Garrison Chief Clerk.

translations.literal: He bore Yuanyou; Yuanyou bore Dang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yuanyou, and Yuanyou's son was Dang.

sentences.zh: 鑒字神具，後魏東徐州刺史、安平康侯。

translations.literal: Jian was styled Shenju, Governor of Eastern Xuzhou under Later Wei and Marquis Kang of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, styled Shenju, served Later Wei as Governor of Eastern Xuzhou and held the title Marquis Kang of Anping.

translations.literal: Three sons: Han, Bingde, and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Han, Bingde, and Xi.

sentences.zh: 秉德，驃騎大將軍，謚曰靖穆。

translations.literal: Bingde, General of Agile Cavalry; his posthumous title was Jingmu.
translations.idiomatic: Bingde served as General of Agile Cavalry; his posthumous title was Jingmu.

translations.literal: Sons: Xin, Junzhe, and Zhongzhe.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Xin, Junzhe, and Zhongzhe.

sentences.zh: 第二房崔氏：琨字景龍，饒陽令，行本郡太守。

translations.literal: The Second Branch Cui clan: Kun was styled Jinglong, Magistrate of Raoyang, acting Governor of the home commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Second Branch Cui clan: Kun, styled Jinglong, served as Magistrate of Raoyang and acting Governor of his home commandery.

translations.literal: Two sons: Jing and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Jing and Yu.

sentences.zh: 經生辯，字神通，後魏武邑太守、饒陽侯，謚曰恭。

translations.literal: Jing bore Bian, styled Shentong, Governor of Wuyi under Later Wei and Marquis of Raoyang; his posthumous title was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's son Bian, styled Shentong, served Later Wei as Governor of Wuyi and held the title Marquis of Raoyang; his posthumous title was Gong.

translations.literal: Two sons: Yi and Kai.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Yi and Kai.

translations.literal: Yu served Later Wei as Governor of Puyang and bore Ting.
translations.idiomatic: Yu served Later Wei as Governor of Puyang, and his son was Ting.

sentences.zh: 第三房崔氏：格二子，蕃、潁。

translations.literal: The Third Branch Cui clan: Ge had two sons, Fan and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: The Third Branch Cui clan: Ge had two sons, Fan and Ying.

translations.literal: Fan bore Tianhu.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's son was Tianhu.

translations.literal: In the eighth generation from Ying, his descendant Buyi, Left Supplementation Official.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth generation from Ying, his descendant Buyi served as Left Supplementation Official.

sentences.zh: 崔氏定著十房：一曰鄭州，二曰鄢陵，三曰南祖，四曰清河大房，五曰清河小房，六曰清河青州房，七曰博陵安平房，八曰博陵大房，九曰博陵第二房，十曰博陵第三房。

translations.literal: The Cui clan was definitively established in ten branches: the first called Zhengzhou, the second Yanling, the third the Southern Branch, the fourth the Qinghe Major Branch, the fifth the Qinghe Minor Branch, the sixth the Qinghe Qingzhou Branch, the seventh the Boling Anping Branch, the eighth the Boling Major Branch, the ninth the Boling Second Branch, and the tenth the Boling Third Branch.
translations.idiomatic: The Cui clan was definitively divided into ten branches: Zhengzhou, Yanling, the Southern Branch, the Qinghe Major Branch, the Qinghe Minor Branch, the Qinghe Qingzhou Branch, the Boling Anping Branch, the Boling Major Branch, the Boling Second Branch, and the Boling Third Branch.

translations.literal: Twenty-three chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: They produced twenty-three chief ministers.

translations.literal: The Zhengzhou Cui clan had Yuanzong;
translations.idiomatic: The Zhengzhou Cui clan produced Yuanzong;

translations.literal: Yanling had Zhiwen;
translations.idiomatic: Yanling produced Zhiwen;

sentences.zh: 南祖有昭緯、慎由、胤、詧、神基；

translations.literal: The Southern Branch had Zhaowei, Shenyou, Yin, Cha, and Shenji;
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Branch produced Zhaowei, Shenyou, Yin, Cha, and Shenji;

sentences.zh: 清河大房有龜從，小房有彥昭、羣、鄲；

translations.literal: The Qinghe Major Branch had Guicong; the Minor Branch had Yanzhao, Qun, and Tan;
translations.idiomatic: The Qinghe Major Branch produced Guicong; the Minor Branch produced Yanzhao, Qun, and Tan;

translations.literal: The Qingzhou Branch had Yuan;
translations.idiomatic: The Qingzhou Branch produced Yuan;

translations.literal: The Anping Branch had Renshi and Shi;
translations.idiomatic: The Anping Branch produced Renshi and Shi;

sentences.zh: 博陵大房有玄暐、損、鉉、元式，第二房有珙、遠、祐甫、植，第三房有日用。

translations.literal: The Boling Major Branch had Xuanwei, Sun, Xuan, and Yuanshi; the Second Branch had Gong, Yuan, Youfu, and Zhi; the Third Branch had Riyong.
translations.idiomatic: The Boling Major Branch produced Xuanwei, Sun, Xuan, and Yuanshi; the Second Branch produced Gong, Yuan, Youfu, and Zhi; and the Third Branch produced Riyong.

translations.literal: The Yu clan of the Yu surname was traced to the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Yu clan descended from the Ji surname.

sentences.zh: 周武王第二子邘叔，子孫以國為氏，其後去「邑」為于氏。

translations.literal: King Wu of Zhou's second son was Yu Shu; his descendants took their state as clan name, and later dropped the character for "settlement" to become the Yu clan.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu of Zhou's second son Yu Shu was enfeoffed at Yu; his descendants took the state as their clan name, and later dropped the "settlement" radical to become the Yu clan.

sentences.zh: 其後自東海郯縣隨拓拔隣徙代，改為萬紐于氏。

translations.literal: Later, from Tan County in Donghai, they followed Tuoba Lin in migrating to Dai and changed their name to the Wan Niuyu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Later, from Tan County in Donghai, they followed Tuoba Lin in migrating to Dai and adopted the surname Wan Niuyu.

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowen of Later Wei, it was restored to the Yu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen of Later Wei, the surname was restored to Yu.

sentences.zh: 外都大官新安公栗磾生侍中、尚書令洛拔。

translations.literal: Li Di, Duke of Xin'an and Director of Outer Court Affairs, bore Luoba, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Di, Duke of Xin'an, served as Director of Outer Court Affairs and had a son Luoba, who served as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 洛拔六子：烈、敦、果、勁、洎、天恩。

translations.literal: Luoba had six sons: Lie, Dun, Guo, Jin, Ji, and Tian'en.
translations.idiomatic: Luoba had six sons: Lie, Dun, Guo, Jin, Ji, and Tian'en.

sentences.zh: 天恩，內行長、遼西太守，生太中大夫仁。

translations.literal: Tian'en served as Inner Bureau Chief and Governor of Liaoxi; he bore Ren, Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Tian'en served as Inner Bureau Chief and Governor of Liaoxi; his son Ren served as Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

translations.literal: Ren bore Zi'an, Commandery General of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Ren's son Zi'an served as Commandery General of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 子安生隴西郡守建平郡公子提。

translations.literal: Zi'an bore Ziti, Administrator of Longxi Commandery and Duke of Jianping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zi'an's son Ziti served as Administrator of Longxi Commandery and held the title Duke of Jianping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 子提生謹，字思敬，從西魏孝武帝入關，遂為京兆長安人，仕後周，太師、燕文公。

translations.literal: Ziti bore Jin, styled Sijing; following Emperor Xiaowu of Western Wei into Guanzhong, he thus became a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao; serving Northern Zhou, he was Grand Preceptor and Duke Wen of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Ziti's son Jin, styled Sijing, followed Emperor Xiaowu of Western Wei into Guanzhong and thus became a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao; serving Northern Zhou, he rose to Grand Preceptor and Duke Wen of Yan.

sentences.zh: 九子：寔、翼、義、智、紹、弼、簡、禮、廣。

translations.literal: Nine sons: Shi, Yi, Yi, Zhi, Shao, Bi, Jian, Li, and Guang.
translations.idiomatic: He had nine sons: Shi, Yi, Yi, Zhi, Shao, Bi, Jian, Li, and Guang.

translations.literal: Of the Yu clan, three chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Yu clan produced three chief ministers.

translations.literal: Di, Zhining, and Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Di, Zhining, and Cong.
